display_title: [XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

Whether a computation is embedded cannot be determined from its direct callers
alone: a `while`, `conditional`, or `call` body inside a `map`, `sort`, or
`reduce` has a `CallContext::kControlFlow` direct caller even though it executes
inside an embedded computation. `CallGraph` already computes transitive
`CallContext` in one pass over the module.

- Add `CallGraphNode::IsEmbedded()` to check whether a computation is in an
  embedded context (`CallContext::kEmbedded` or `CallContext::kBoth`).
- Use `CallGraphNode::IsEmbedded()` in `InstructionFusion`, `MultiOutputFusion`,
  and `EmbeddedWhileLoopUnroller` instead of
  `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.
- Add `ScatterExpander::kEliminateEmbeddedScatters` backed by `CallGraph` and
  use it in `CpuCompiler` so transitively embedded scatters are expanded too.
- Remove `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.

Note on behavior change: this is not purely a refactor for non-CPU backends.
Control-flow bodies nested inside embedded computations (e.g. a `while`,
`conditional`, or `call` inside a `reduce`/`sort`/`map` body) were previously
fused by `InstructionFusion` and `MultiOutputFusion` on GPU/TPU and now will not
be.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Order producer-consumer adaptor instructions like the fused fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Order producer-consumer adaptor instructions like the fused fusion

`HloFusionAdaptor::MakeInstructionPostOrder()` returned the producer's
instructions followed by the consumer's. The fused computation visits the
producer where the consumer first reads it, after the consumer instructions
that come before that operand. The two orders differ for
`add(reduce(a), producer)`.

Instead, the adaptor now walks the producer and the consumer depth-first from
the fusion roots, like the post order of the fused computation. This also
covers producers with several outputs.

This is needed for correctness because the config for sequential dimensions relies on the positional information.

display_title: Move the XLA:CPU builtin symbols to an LLVM-free target

head_commit.message:
Move the XLA:CPU builtin symbols to an LLVM-free target

The table of host functions that XLA:CPU kernels can call (libm, fp16 and bf16 conversions, __powisf2, ...) lives inside `BuiltinDefinitionGenerator`, which is an ORC definition generator, so loaders that don't use ORC can't reuse it.

So we move the table to `:builtin_symbols` (`FindBuiltinSymbol`), which doesn't depend on LLVM, and `BuiltinDefinitionGenerator` looks names up there. That way ORC and `LiteObjectLoader` (next CLs) resolve exactly the same symbols.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Preserve gpu_device_info.name in GpuTargetConfig::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Preserve gpu_device_info.name in GpuTargetConfig::FromProto

`GpuTargetConfig::FromProto` unconditionally overwrote `device_description.name`
with `device_description_str` whenever `device_description_str` was non-empty
(a fallback introduced before `GpuDeviceInfoProto` had a `name` field). For
specs where the two fields differ (currently `specs/b300.txtpb`, with
`name: "NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC"` and `device_description_str: "NVIDIA B300"`), this
silently mutated `gpu_device_info.name` across a `FromProto`/`ToProto`
round-trip, broke `DeviceDescription::EqualsTo` against a live B300, and caused
`device_description.name()` consumers (e.g., `FormatDevicePropertiesJson`,
`CubScratchSizeDevicelessLookup`) to see `device_description_str` instead.

Only fall back to `device_description_str` when `device_description.name()` is
empty or `se::DeviceDescription::kUndefinedString`, matching the existing
`runtime_version` fallback directly below it. All other checked-in GPU target
specs either omit `gpu_device_info.name` or set both fields identically, so
their behavior is unchanged.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support split M dimensions in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support split M dimensions in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

When the non-contracting dimension of the left-hand side of a dot consists of two strided segments of a parameter (it's split), we can assign the major segment to be a batch dimension in cuDNN. This only works if there isn't a batch dimension already.

All tensors of the LHS and of the dot itself then must be split in the same way, so that the cuDNN graph has a consistent batch dimension; tensors that are broadcasted along M are left as is.

This is the final change before we can swap out TritonFusionAnalysis from Cudnn Gemm Fusion.

display_title: [XLA] Prevent int64_t overflow in AxisRef sub-axis next_pre_size

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Prevent int64_t overflow in AxisRef sub-axis next_pre_size

`AxisRef::SubAxis::next_pre_size()` computes `pre_size * size` with unchecked signed 64-bit multiplication. Large `pre_size` and `size` values can overflow `int64_t`, wrapping to `0` (triggering `SIGFPE` in `AxisRef::Validate` and `CanCoexistWithoutOverlap`) or wrapping to a small divisor of the axis size (bypassing `AxisRef::Validate` and causing an out-of-bounds write to `transpose_perm` in `HloSharding::V3ToV2Sharding`).

Add `AxisRef::ValidateSubAxis(int64_t pre_size, int64_t size)` using `OverflowSafeMultiply` and enforce it in the `AxisRef` sub-axis constructor so every live `AxisRef` has a representable `next_pre_size()`. Validate sub-axes before construction in `HloParserImpl::ParseAxisRef` and `mhlo_to_hlo`'s `BuildAxisRefs` to return clean errors on invalid inputs, and add bounds `CHECK_LT` guards on `transpose_perm` writes in `HloSharding::V3ToV2Sharding`.

head_commit.message:
PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52971

#ai-generated

Fixes #52968.

## Status quo

`HandleDivide` rewrites floating-point division by a constant into multiplication by a rounded reciprocal, including when `enable_fast_math` is false.

## Why

We encountered this while comparing an ONNX quantized MLP across execution backends. For float32 `[-100, 0.1, 100]`, the scale `200 / 255` changes by one ULP. The subsequent zero-point calculation crosses a rounding boundary, producing 127 instead of 128. The issue includes an independent JAX reproduction with CPU fast math disabled.

## Design choices

Require `enable_fast_math` for this rewrite in `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor` via a virtual protected `ShouldRewriteDivideByConstantToMultiply()` hook (which returns `options_.enable_fast_math()` by default) so subclasses can override the policy independently. Add scalar and broadcasted-constant tests with fast math disabled, and explicitly enable fast math in the existing reciprocal-rewrite tests.

In `xla/service/cpu/tests/onednn_matmul_test.cc`, enable CPU fast math in `DivisionByConstantWithEltwiseLinearF32` (since oneDNN `LINEAR` post-op fusion relies on `AlgebraicSimplifier` rewriting constant division to multiplication) and add `DivisionByConstantWithoutFastMathNotFusedF32` to verify that division remains unfused when fast math is disabled.

## Trade-offs

This retains the rewrite in fast-math mode. With fast math disabled, it preserves division and may reduce strength-reduction opportunities outside backends or passes that opt in via `ShouldRewriteDivideByConstantToMultiply()`.

## Testing

All tests in `//xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test` pass.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix shared_ptr lifetime race in NcclCommunicatorTest.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix shared_ptr lifetime race in NcclCommunicatorTest.

In AcquireSymmetricMemory Promise::Set wakes Await() before the worker threads unwind and Promise objects detroyed.
Therefore worker threads could still hold extra shared_ptr<SymmetricMemory> copies after the helper returned. That caused flakiness in AcquireSymmetricMemoryCachesByAddress during use_count() check.

Switch AcquireSymmetricMemory to exec.Execute with an absl::BlockingCounter so each worker writes its result directly into the caller's vector.

Also check window destruction via `std::weak_ptr::expired()` after `ReleaseSymmetricMemory` and `bigger.clear()` instead of inspecting `use_count()`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Preserve gpu_device_info.name in GpuTargetConfig::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Preserve gpu_device_info.name in GpuTargetConfig::FromProto

`GpuTargetConfig::FromProto` unconditionally overwrote `device_description.name`
with `device_description_str` whenever `device_description_str` was non-empty
(a fallback introduced before `GpuDeviceInfoProto` had a `name` field). For
specs where the two fields differ (currently `specs/b300.txtpb`, with
`name: "NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC"` and `device_description_str: "NVIDIA B300"`), this
silently mutated `gpu_device_info.name` across a `FromProto`/`ToProto`
round-trip, broke `DeviceDescription::EqualsTo` against a live B300, and caused
`device_description.name()` consumers (e.g., `FormatDevicePropertiesJson`,
`CubScratchSizeDevicelessLookup`) to see `device_description_str` instead.

Only fall back to `device_description_str` when `device_description.name()` is
empty or `se::DeviceDescription::kUndefinedString`, matching the existing
`runtime_version` fallback directly below it. All other checked-in GPU target
specs either omit `gpu_device_info.name` or set both fields identically, so
their behavior is unchanged.

display_title: [XLA] Fix int64 truncation in IotaTileAssignment::value_at

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix int64 truncation in IotaTileAssignment::value_at

`IotaTileAssignment::value_at` stored each `int64_t` reshape dimension in an
`int`. Reshape dimensions are only validated to be non-negative with a
non-overflowing product, so a dimension of 2^32 truncated to 0 (division by
zero), 2^31 truncated to INT_MIN (negative device ids), and other values above
INT_MAX silently produced wrong device ids.

Keep the dimension size as `int64_t`, matching `index_for`, and add tests with
reshape dimensions above INT_MAX.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support split M dimensions in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support split M dimensions in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

When the non-contracting dimension of the left-hand side of a dot consists of two strided segments of a parameter (it's split), we can assign the major segment to be a batch dimension in cuDNN. This only works if there isn't a batch dimension already.

All tensors of the LHS and of the dot itself then must be split in the same way, so that the cuDNN graph has a consistent batch dimension; tensors that are broadcasted along M are left as is.

This is the final change before we can swap out TritonFusionAnalysis from Cudnn Gemm Fusion.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [ROCm] Split decode-shaped dots on gfx950 that the default split-K weights leave unsplit

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Split decode-shaped dots on gfx950 that the default split-K weights leave unsplit

GetCostWeights only has CUDA weights, so gfx950 uses the pre-Hopper ones.
Their fixed reduction cost keeps decode GEMMs (few rows, long K) unsplit
even when the unsplit output leaves most CUs idle.

On gfx950, when the default weights pick no split, re-cost the dot with
gfx950 weights if it is unbatched, has at most 32 rows, K >= 2048, at
least 1 MiB of RHS, and its unsplit output tiles fill at most half the
cores. Every other dot keeps the current decision, as do CUDA and the
other ROCm GPUs.

Using the gfx950 weights for every dot picked slower splits on batched,
small and short-K dots, on outputs that already fill most of the GPU,
and when raising a split the default weights already make.

display_title: [XLA] Prevent int64_t overflow in AxisRef sub-axis next_pre_size

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Prevent int64_t overflow in AxisRef sub-axis next_pre_size

`AxisRef::SubAxis::next_pre_size()` computes `pre_size * size` with unchecked signed 64-bit multiplication. Large `pre_size` and `size` values can overflow `int64_t`, wrapping to `0` (triggering `SIGFPE` in `AxisRef::Validate` and `CanCoexistWithoutOverlap`) or wrapping to a small divisor of the axis size (bypassing `AxisRef::Validate` and causing an out-of-bounds write to `transpose_perm` in `HloSharding::V3ToV2Sharding`).

Add `AxisRef::ValidateSubAxis(int64_t pre_size, int64_t size)` using `OverflowSafeMultiply` and enforce it in the `AxisRef` sub-axis constructor so every live `AxisRef` has a representable `next_pre_size()`. Validate sub-axes before construction in `HloParserImpl::ParseAxisRef` and `mhlo_to_hlo`'s `BuildAxisRefs` to return clean errors on invalid inputs, and add bounds `CHECK_LT` guards on `transpose_perm` writes in `HloSharding::V3ToV2Sharding`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

`RecordKernelLaunch` unconditionally prepended `ctx->dependencies` even when a handler passed explicit `dependencies`. In a multi-command `Record` handler, chained launches got redundant direct edges from preceding thunks (and spurious programmatic edges when `uses_pdl` was set). Conversely, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D` and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand` ignored `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, leaving root memcpy and empty commands without edges from preceding thunks, and skipped null checks on `ctx`, `out_command`, and `dependencies`.

Share a single `ResolveDependencies` helper across `RecordKernelLaunch`, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D`, and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand`: inherit `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, and validate and forward only the caller-specified commands when `num_dependencies > 0`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1028111444

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52878

## Summary

This change makes the MORI GPU collectives backend serve XLA's GXL
ragged-all-to-all / all-gather hook and adds async start/done support to the
MORI communicator, so ragged-all-to-all and other MORI collectives can be
issued on an async stream and overlapped by the latency-hiding scheduler.

It is gated behind the existing `--xla_gpu_enable_gxl_ragged_all_to_all` flag
and only takes effect when the collectives implementation is MORI
(`--xla_gpu_collectives_implementation=mori`); the default NCCL/RCCL path is
unchanged.

## Motivation

`RaggedAllToAllThunk` previously only had the symmetric-memory and peer-access
kernel strategies. MORI already implements a fast SDMA-push ragged-all-to-all
in the `CollectivesFacade`, but there was no way for the thunk to call into it.
I decided to reuse already existing `GxlCommunicator` interface (`RunAllGatherGxl`,
`RunRaggedAllToAllGxl`) for exactly this purpose, reached via
`GpuCommunicator::gxl_communicator()`. This PR implements that hook for MORI and
teaches the ragged-all-to-all thunk to delegate to it.

This way, we **do not need to add anything specific** to RaggedAllToAllThunk which is already quite complex.
There are just _two general fixes_ in RaggedAllToAllThunk related to GXL communicator handling.

## What changed

### GXL hook (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`)

- `MoriCommunicator` now overrides `gxl_communicator()` and owns a nested
  `GxlAdapter` (a `GxlCommunicator` holding a back-pointer to the communicator).
  Using a member adapter rather than multiple inheritance keeps the
  `GpuCommunicator`/`GxlCommunicator` hierarchies separate.
- `GxlAdapter::RunAllGatherGxl` forwards to `LaunchAllGather`;
  `RunRaggedAllToAllGxl` forwards to the new `LaunchRaggedAllToAll`.

### Ragged-all-to-all thunk (`ragged_all_to_all_thunk.cc`)

- `Initialize`: when `enable_gxl` is set and the clique's communicator exposes a
  GXL communicator, return early — the GXL path runs the whole op, so no kernel
  or NCCL-fallback state is allocated (kernel strategy stays `kNone`).
- `Record`: under the same condition, delegate to `CollectiveThunk::Record`,
  which traces `RunCollective` and dispatches to the GXL communicator.

### Async start/done (`mori_communicator.{h,cc}`, `mori_kernels.h`)

- Added `SetAsync(bool)` / `AsyncDone(executor)` and an internal
  `LaunchOrDefer` helper. These is a preparation for MORI async collectives support, **not wired yet**.
- Removed the old `Execute` wrapper; the `Launch*` methods are called directly.

### Build / misc

- Renamed the MORI facade namespace usages from `mori::collective` to
  `mori::ccl` to match the repinned MORI headers.

### MORI repin (`third_party/roc_mori/workspace.bzl`)

- Repinned `@roc_mori` to MORI tag `xla-pin-20261112`
  (commit `d50338eb5f45d4338ee64ef27fa7f22a71638b9f`) with the matching archive
  `sha256`.

## Testing

- `RaggedAllToAll_2GPUs_CommandBuffer/async_nccl_fallback_peer` passes,
  exercising the async + command-buffer path end-to-end through the MORI GXL
  hook.
- Verified on a MaxText Mixtral-8x7b MoE run (expert-parallel, EP=8) that the
  MORI ragged-all-to-all kernel is selected and produces correct results; the
  collective runs at the standalone benchmark's bandwidth when ranks arrive
  together.

display_title: [XLA] Use int64_t accumulator in DimensionSharding::getShardedSize

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use int64_t accumulator in DimensionSharding::getShardedSize

`NamedSharding::DimensionSharding::getShardedSize` passed a 32-bit `int`
literal `1` to `std::accumulate`, narrowing the `int64_t` product to 32-bit
`int` on each iteration. For valid `NamedSharding`s whose dimension sharding
product reaches 2^31 or higher, this could wrap to negative values, truncate to
0 (causing division-by-zero crashes in `TileShape` and `ReplicationFactor` or
`CHECK` failures in `V3ToV2Sharding`), or truncate to 1 (causing
`IsReplicated()` to silently return true).

Switch to `absl::c_accumulate` with `int64_t{1}` so the full 64-bit product is
preserved, and add unit tests covering sharded sizes >= 2^31.

display_title: [XLA] Remove prime factorization from IotaTileAssignment::Transpose

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove prime factorization from IotaTileAssignment::Transpose

IotaTileAssignment::Transpose split reshape dims into prime factors by trial
division with a 32-bit counter. Large prime dims (e.g. from a deserialized
OpSharding) overflowed the counter and looped forever, and even a 64-bit counter
made trial division up to sqrt(2^62) a multi-second CPU cost. Zero-sized dims
also looped forever.

Transpose only needs the shortest common refinement of the tile dims and the
transposed reshape dims, which GetOrderedSubDims already computes in linear time
using divisibility checks. Use it instead, canonicalize zero-element iota tile
assignments in TryCreate, short-circuit Transpose for them, and make
ExtractCommonFactorSequence reject non-positive sizes instead of dividing by
zero.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bound iota materialization in HloSharding::FromProto

A few-byte iota `OpSharding` can describe billions of devices. When its
replicated or subgroup dimensions do not align with the iota reshape
dimensions, `TryPartialTile` and `TrySubgroup` fall back to materializing an
explicit `Array<int64_t>`, so a tiny proto could allocate tens of GiB inside
`HloSharding::FromProto`.

`FromProto` now charges these iota-to-array fallbacks against a budget of 2^16
elements shared across all tuple elements, and returns InvalidArgument once it
is exceeded. Small non-aligned iota shardings still deserialize as before, and
the public `TryPartialTile`/`TrySubgroup` factories stay unlimited. `TrySubgroup`
now propagates `TryPartialTile` errors instead of CHECK-failing, and its
explicit-array fallback uses a single transpose instead of per-element index
vectors.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

`RecordKernelLaunch` unconditionally prepended `ctx->dependencies` even when a handler passed explicit `dependencies`. In a multi-command `Record` handler, chained launches got redundant direct edges from preceding thunks (and spurious programmatic edges when `uses_pdl` was set). Conversely, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D` and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand` ignored `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, leaving root memcpy and empty commands without edges from preceding thunks, and skipped null checks on `ctx`, `out_command`, and `dependencies`.

Share a single `ResolveDependencies` helper across `RecordKernelLaunch`, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D`, and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand`: inherit `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, and validate and forward only the caller-specified commands when `num_dependencies > 0`.

`GetCompilerIr` with `OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED` returned

the executable's optimized HloModule and `buffer_assignment_proto()` instead.
On CPU, literal payloads are still stripped, as the CPU compiler did when it
embedded the proto.

The output doesn't change, except that backends which never embedded an
HloProto no longer crash here. (With `--xla_dump_to` set, this used to return
the HloModule before optimizations; XLA already fixed that when it stopped
replacing the executable's HloProto for HLO snapshots.)

display_title: [XLA] Prevent int64_t overflow in AxisRef sub-axis next_pre_size

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Prevent int64_t overflow in AxisRef sub-axis next_pre_size

`AxisRef::SubAxis::next_pre_size()` computes `pre_size * size` with unchecked signed 64-bit multiplication. Large `pre_size` and `size` values can overflow `int64_t`, wrapping to `0` (triggering `SIGFPE` in `AxisRef::Validate` and `CanCoexistWithoutOverlap`) or wrapping to a small divisor of the axis size (bypassing `AxisRef::Validate` and causing an out-of-bounds write to `transpose_perm` in `HloSharding::V3ToV2Sharding`).

Add `AxisRef::ValidateSubAxis(int64_t pre_size, int64_t size)` using `OverflowSafeMultiply` and enforce it in the `AxisRef` sub-axis constructor so every live `AxisRef` has a representable `next_pre_size()`. Validate sub-axes before construction in `HloParserImpl::ParseAxisRef` and `mhlo_to_hlo`'s `BuildAxisRefs` to return clean errors on invalid inputs, and add bounds `CHECK_LT` guards on `transpose_perm` writes in `HloSharding::V3ToV2Sharding`.

display_title: Stop calling Executable::set_hlo_proto in the GPU and CPU compilers

head_commit.message:
Stop calling Executable::set_hlo_proto in the GPU and CPU compilers

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The GPU and CPU compilers only attached an `HloProto` so that the
base class could answer `buffer_assignment_proto()` and so that HLO snapshots
had something to read. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` now override
`buffer_assignment_proto()` themselves, and snapshots no longer read
`Executable::hlo_proto()`, so the compilers stop calling `set_hlo_proto`.

`Executable::hlo_proto()` now returns nullptr for GPU and CPU executables. No
caller in XLA reads it anymore. `buffer_assignment_proto()` returns the same as
before.

display_title: [XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

📝 Summary of Changes

PR #52906 restricted HandleMaximum's maximum(a, clamp(a, x, b)) -> clamp(a, x, b) rewrite using IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (via HloEvaluator and ComparisonDirection::kLe).
That still leaves several issues:
- +0.0 <= -0.0 evaluates to true under partial order, folding max(+0.0, clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0)) to clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0) (-0.0 instead of +0.0).
- Building a kLt/kLe kCompare and calling HloEvaluator::Evaluate aborts AlgebraicSimplifier::Run() with UnimplementedError on complex bounds (c64/c128) and TF_RET_CHECK-fails on mixed-FP bounds (both in HandleMaximum and in MinMaxToClamp).
- IsKnownLessThanOrEqual folds lhs == rhs unconditionally and allocates a fresh HloEvaluator on every match.

This change replaces IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (and HloEvaluator in MinMaxToClamp) with a shared CompareConstantBounds helper that checks matching, non-complex array element types and evaluates strict lower < upper directly on the scalar literals via PrimitiveTypeSwitch and Comparison, removing the hlo_evaluator dependency from algebraic_simplifier. Degenerate equal-bound clamps (a == b) are not worth special-casing, matching MinMaxToClamp.

🎯 Justification

Follow-up to #52659 / #52906: prevents sign-bit flips on (+0.0, -0.0) clamp bounds, prevents AlgebraicSimplifier pass failures on complex or mixed-precision bounds, and avoids HloEvaluator overhead during simplification.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc:
- MaxOfClamp: ordered constant bounds (0 and 6); expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithBroadcastBounds: broadcast ordered bounds with maximum operands swapped; expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithUnorderedBounds: constant bounds 10 and 0; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithParameterBounds: runtime parameter bounds; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithSignedZeroBounds: constant bounds +0.0 and -0.0; expects no change (fails with a <= check).
- MaxOfClampWithComplexBounds: c64 constant bounds; expects no change without failing.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

display_title: [XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

📝 Summary of Changes

PR #52906 restricted HandleMaximum's maximum(a, clamp(a, x, b)) -> clamp(a, x, b) rewrite using IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (via HloEvaluator and ComparisonDirection::kLe).
That still leaves several issues:
- +0.0 <= -0.0 evaluates to true under partial order, folding max(+0.0, clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0)) to clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0) (-0.0 instead of +0.0).
- Building a kLt/kLe kCompare and calling HloEvaluator::Evaluate aborts AlgebraicSimplifier::Run() with UnimplementedError on complex bounds (c64/c128) and TF_RET_CHECK-fails on mixed-FP bounds (both in HandleMaximum and in MinMaxToClamp).
- IsKnownLessThanOrEqual folds lhs == rhs unconditionally and allocates a fresh HloEvaluator on every match.

This change replaces IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (and HloEvaluator in MinMaxToClamp) with a shared CompareConstantBounds helper that checks matching, non-complex array element types and evaluates strict lower < upper directly on the scalar literals via PrimitiveTypeSwitch and Comparison, removing the hlo_evaluator dependency from algebraic_simplifier. Degenerate equal-bound clamps (a == b) are not worth special-casing, matching MinMaxToClamp.

🎯 Justification

Follow-up to #52659 / #52906: prevents sign-bit flips on (+0.0, -0.0) clamp bounds, prevents AlgebraicSimplifier pass failures on complex or mixed-precision bounds, and avoids HloEvaluator overhead during simplification.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc:
- MaxOfClamp: ordered constant bounds (0 and 6); expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithBroadcastBounds: broadcast ordered bounds with maximum operands swapped; expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithUnorderedBounds: constant bounds 10 and 0; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithParameterBounds: runtime parameter bounds; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithSignedZeroBounds: constant bounds +0.0 and -0.0; expects no change (fails with a <= check).
- MaxOfClampWithComplexBounds: c64 constant bounds; expects no change without failing.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

`RecordKernelLaunch` unconditionally prepended `ctx->dependencies` even when a handler passed explicit `dependencies`. In a multi-command `Record` handler, chained launches got redundant direct edges from preceding thunks (and spurious programmatic edges when `uses_pdl` was set). Conversely, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D` and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand` ignored `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, leaving root memcpy and empty commands without edges from preceding thunks, and skipped null checks on `ctx`, `out_command`, and `dependencies`.

Share a single `ResolveDependencies` helper across `RecordKernelLaunch`, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D`, and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand`: inherit `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, and validate and forward only the caller-specified commands when `num_dependencies > 0`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1027978294

display_title: [XLA] Avoid int32 overflow in IotaTileAssignment::size_bytes()

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Avoid int32 overflow in IotaTileAssignment::size_bytes()

`IotaTileAssignment::size_bytes()` previously computed the backing buffer size in signed 32-bit `int`, while `ValidateIotaDims` permits ranks up to `INT_MAX`. For large ranks (e.g., `2^29`), `size_bytes()` could wrap to a small positive value, causing an undersized heap allocation followed by an out-of-bounds `std::memcpy`.

Compute `size_bytes()` and copy-assignment sizes in `size_t`, bound the validated rank against `std::ptrdiff_t` overflow on 32-bit platforms, fix a signed `int` addition overflow in `CanonicalizeIotaDims`, and make `IotaTileAssignment` move/copy/self-assignment safe for moved-from instances.

head_commit.message:
PR #53101: [ROCm] Non-temporal cache hints for gfx942

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53101

📝 Summary of Changes
On MI300, MLIR kernels mark large streamed loads and stores non-temporal. Loads need a buffer of at least 16×L2 (64 MiB) that is read once; stores need one qualifying output in a contiguous kernel.

🎯 Justification
Data touched once otherwise evicts reused data from L2 and from MI300X's Infinity Cache. This helps memory-bound fusions over large buffers.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: ⚡️ Performance Improvement, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Synthetic streaming kernels of 64–512 MiB average −11.5%.

🧪 Unit Tests:
nontemporal_hints_test.cc,  lower_tensors_amdgpu_nontemporal.mlir, mlir_kernel_emitter_test.cc

display_title: PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

head_commit.message:
PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52971

#ai-generated

Fixes #52968.

## Status quo

`HandleDivide` rewrites floating-point division by a constant into multiplication by a rounded reciprocal, including when `enable_fast_math` is false.

## Why

We encountered this while comparing an ONNX quantized MLP across execution backends. For float32 `[-100, 0.1, 100]`, the scale `200 / 255` changes by one ULP. The subsequent zero-point calculation crosses a rounding boundary, producing 127 instead of 128. The issue includes an independent JAX reproduction with CPU fast math disabled.

## Design choices

Require `enable_fast_math` for this rewrite. Add scalar and broadcasted-constant tests with fast math disabled, and explicitly enable fast math in the existing reciprocal-rewrite tests.

## Trade-offs

This retains the rewrite in fast-math mode. With fast math disabled, it preserves division and may reduce strength-reduction opportunities. Performance impact has not been benchmarked.

## Testing

The two new regression tests fail against the original implementation. With the fix, all 2,069 tests in `algebraic_simplifier_test` pass locally using Bazel 8.8.2 and Clang 21 on Linux x86-64.

The broader `bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/...` run also passes all 50 test targets.

display_title: Move the XLA:CPU builtin symbols to an LLVM-free target

head_commit.message:
Move the XLA:CPU builtin symbols to an LLVM-free target

The table of host functions that XLA:CPU kernels can call (libm, fp16 and bf16 conversions, __powisf2, ...) lives inside `BuiltinDefinitionGenerator`, which is an ORC definition generator, so loaders that don't use ORC can't reuse it.

So we move the table to `:builtin_symbols` (`FindBuiltinSymbol`), which doesn't depend on LLVM, and `BuiltinDefinitionGenerator` looks names up there. That way ORC and `LiteObjectLoader` (next CLs) resolve exactly the same symbols.

display_title: Move StripPayloadFromLiteralProto to xla/service/hlo_proto_util.h

head_commit.message:
Move StripPayloadFromLiteralProto to xla/service/hlo_proto_util.h

`StripPayloadFromLiteralProto` drops the literal payloads from an `HloProto`
but keeps their shapes. It was declared in
`xla/service/cpu/cpu_aot_compilation_result.h` because only the CPU compiler
used it. TF's `get_compiler_ir` needs it as well once it stops reading
`Executable::hlo_proto()`, so move it next to `MakeHloProto` (and from
namespace `xla::cpu` to `xla`).

This is part of removing `Executable::hlo_proto_`, so that `Executable` can
become an abstract base class without data members and loading an
AOT-compiled executable doesn't need to build the HloModule.

No behaviour change.

display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.
- Disables SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes cl/959445928, i.e.
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use A100 instead of V100 in cuDNN deviceless fusion tests.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use A100 instead of V100 in cuDNN deviceless fusion tests.

cuDNN 9.11 dropped execution support for compute capability below 7.5 (Volta and older). cuDNN Frontend v1.33.0 now declines SM70 targets up front in `create_execution_plans` and `check_support`. Because `CudnnFusionCompilerDevicelessTest` requires cuDNN 9.15 or newer, probing `GpuModel::V100` (sm_70) now returns `kUnsupported` for plain f32 convolutions. That SM floor also masks the FP8 check in `Fp8ConvVerdictTracksTargetGpu`.

display_title: [XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject out-of-range 64-bit transpose_perm in IotaTileAssignment

`MeshProto::IotaTransform::transpose_perm` stores `int64` entries, but
`IotaTileAssignment::Create(dims, transform)` copied them directly into `int`
before validation. Out-of-range 64-bit values whose low 32 bits formed a valid
permutation (for example `[4294967297, 4294967296]`) were silently truncated
and accepted instead of rejected.

Add `IotaTileAssignment::TryCreate(dims, const MeshProto::IotaTransform&)` to
range-check each 64-bit `transpose_perm` entry against `[0, perm_size)` before
narrowing to `int`, and delegate `Create(dims, transform)` to `TryCreate`.

display_title: [XLA] Use int64_t accumulator in DimensionSharding::getShardedSize

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use int64_t accumulator in DimensionSharding::getShardedSize

`NamedSharding::DimensionSharding::getShardedSize` passed a 32-bit `int`
literal `1` to `std::accumulate`, narrowing the `int64_t` product to 32-bit
`int` on each iteration. For valid `NamedSharding`s whose dimension sharding
product reaches 2^31 or higher, this could wrap to negative values, truncate to
0 (causing division-by-zero crashes in `TileShape` and `ReplicationFactor` or
`CHECK` failures in `V3ToV2Sharding`), or truncate to 1 (causing
`IsReplicated()` to silently return true).

Switch to `absl::c_accumulate` with `int64_t{1}` so the full 64-bit product is
preserved, and add unit tests covering sharded sizes >= 2^31.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix int64 truncation in IotaTileAssignment::value_at

`IotaTileAssignment::value_at` stored each `int64_t` reshape dimension in an
`int`. Reshape dimensions are only validated to be non-negative with a
non-overflowing product, so a dimension of 2^32 truncated to 0 (division by
zero), 2^31 truncated to INT_MIN (negative device ids), and other values above
INT_MAX silently produced wrong device ids.

Keep the dimension size as `int64_t`, matching `index_for`, and add tests with
reshape dimensions above INT_MAX.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use a sorted address index in BufferAllocations::FindAllocationIndex.

FindAllocationIndex used to scan every buffer allocation. Collective FFI
handlers, such as Mosaic GPU kernels, call it for each buffer on every
execution, in both the Prepare and Initialize stages. With thousands of
allocations this can cause an overhead.

The first lookup now sorts the allocations by start address. Later lookups
binary search for the nearest start at or before the address. They then walk
back to the first allocation that fully contains [addr, addr + size). Equal
starts resolve to the lowest index. Lookups are O(log n) when allocations don't
overlap.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Avoid int32 overflow in IotaTileAssignment::size_bytes()

`IotaTileAssignment::size_bytes()` previously computed the backing buffer size in signed 32-bit `int`, while `ValidateIotaDims` permits ranks up to `INT_MAX`. For large ranks (e.g., `2^29`), `size_bytes()` could wrap to a small positive value, causing an undersized heap allocation followed by an out-of-bounds `std::memcpy`.

Compute `size_bytes()` and copy-assignment sizes in `size_t`, bound the validated rank against `std::ptrdiff_t` overflow on 32-bit platforms, fix a signed `int` addition overflow in `CanonicalizeIotaDims`, and make `IotaTileAssignment` move/copy/self-assignment safe for moved-from instances.

display_title: Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

head_commit.message:
Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. `hlo_proto_` on the base mixes up two things: the buffer assignment
that the backend owns, and an HLO snapshot that the creator attaches for
dumping. This CL starts to pull them apart.

`Executable::buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes virtual. The default still
reads `hlo_proto_`. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` override it from state
they own, and return it in exactly the cases where the base accessor returns
non-null today:

- `GpuExecutable` returns its buffer assignment proto only if the compiler
  embeds debug info and keeps the HloModule
  (`Params::expose_buffer_assignment_proto`). Executables loaded from a proto
  still return nullptr. The always-available GPU accessor is renamed to
  `owned_buffer_assignment_proto()`, because a non-virtual accessor with the
  same name would hide the virtual one.
- `CpuExecutable` gets an optional buffer assignment proto that the CPU
  compiler sets with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, and the CPU AOT loader with
  `xla_embed_ir_in_executable` or `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots`.

The compilers still call `set_hlo_proto`; that goes away in a follow-up.

No behaviour change.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

head_commit.message:
Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The HLO that goes into HLO snapshots is debug state of whoever runs
the executable, so it moves out of `Executable::hlo_proto_`:

- `Service::BuildExecutable` returns the HLO before optimizations (plus the
  buffer assignment after optimizations) through an optional out-param instead
  of `set_hlo_proto`. `Service::Compile` keeps it in the `CompilationCache`
  entry, and `Service::Execute` reads it from there.
- `LocalExecutable` gets an optional snapshot HLO, filled through a new
  optional out-param of `LocalService::CompileExecutables`. Executables loaded
  with `LocalClient::Load` don't have one.
- New free helpers in `xla/service/executable.h`: `DumpingHloSnapshots()`
  replaces `Executable::dumping_snapshot()` at these call sites, and
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()` builds the snapshot HLO from the executable's
  HloModule and buffer assignment if nobody kept one.
- The HLO before optimizations is only built if `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots` is
  set, since snapshots are its only reader.
- The CPU AOT loader no longer attaches a full HloProto when dumping snapshots;
  the fallback above produces the same content.
- Deletes the unused `HloRunnerLegacy::HloProtoFromWrapped`.

Behaviour change: snapshot paths that dereferenced a null `hlo_proto()` before
(e.g. CPU without `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, GPU executables loaded from a
proto, `Service::ExecuteGraphParallel` on CPU) now dump the optimized HloModule
instead of crashing. On CPU with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, these snapshots
now keep literal payloads. Snapshots that contain the HLO before optimizations
today still do. Since `Service` no longer replaces the executable's HloProto,
TF's `get_compiler_ir` with `OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED` now returns the
optimized module also when dumping is enabled. It returned the module before
optimizations in that case, which was a bug.

display_title: PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

head_commit.message:
PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52971

#ai-generated

Fixes #52968.

## Status quo

`HandleDivide` rewrites floating-point division by a constant into multiplication by a rounded reciprocal, including when `enable_fast_math` is false.

## Why

We encountered this while comparing an ONNX quantized MLP across execution backends. For float32 `[-100, 0.1, 100]`, the scale `200 / 255` changes by one ULP. The subsequent zero-point calculation crosses a rounding boundary, producing 127 instead of 128. The issue includes an independent JAX reproduction with CPU fast math disabled.

## Design choices

Require `enable_fast_math` for this rewrite. Add scalar and broadcasted-constant tests with fast math disabled, and explicitly enable fast math in the existing reciprocal-rewrite tests.

## Trade-offs

This retains the rewrite in fast-math mode. With fast math disabled, it preserves division and may reduce strength-reduction opportunities. Performance impact has not been benchmarked.

## Testing

The two new regression tests fail against the original implementation. With the fix, all 2,069 tests in `algebraic_simplifier_test` pass locally using Bazel 8.8.2 and Clang 21 on Linux x86-64.

The broader `bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/...` run also passes all 50 test targets.

display_title: [XLA] Prevent int64_t overflow in AxisRef sub-axis next_pre_size

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Prevent int64_t overflow in AxisRef sub-axis next_pre_size

`AxisRef::SubAxis::next_pre_size()` computes `pre_size * size` with unchecked signed 64-bit multiplication. Large `pre_size` and `size` values can overflow `int64_t`, wrapping to `0` (triggering `SIGFPE` in `AxisRef::Validate` and `CanCoexistWithoutOverlap`) or wrapping to a small divisor of the axis size (bypassing `AxisRef::Validate` and causing an out-of-bounds write to `transpose_perm` in `HloSharding::V3ToV2Sharding`).

Add `AxisRef::ValidateSubAxis(int64_t pre_size, int64_t size)` using `OverflowSafeMultiply` and enforce it in the `AxisRef` sub-axis constructor so every live `AxisRef` has a representable `next_pre_size()`. Validate sub-axes before construction in `HloParserImpl::ParseAxisRef` and `mhlo_to_hlo`'s `BuildAxisRefs` to return clean errors on invalid inputs, and add bounds `CHECK_LT` guards on `transpose_perm` writes in `HloSharding::V3ToV2Sharding`.

display_title: PR #53387: [XLA:GPU] Resolve async-start through async intermediaries in LHS GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit

head_commit.message:
PR #53387: [XLA:GPU] Resolve async-start through async intermediaries in LHS GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53387

📝 Summary of Changes

`GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit` was assuming that the async-start corresponding to a candidate async-done is always the done's first operand. This is not the case when the start reaches the done through intermediary instructions (e.g. `tuple`, `opt-barrier`, `get-tuple-element`, etc). This PR uses the `FindStart()` helper to resolve the async-start through intermediaries. If `FindStart` cannot resolve a start in the computation being scheduled, the function conservatively reports that the overlap limit is crossed.

Limitations:
- Overlapping a collective with a loop-carried future is unsupported. This is because `FindStart()` only returns an async-start if the start is in the same computation as the done, which isn't the case with while ops (the done in the body has a start reachable from the caller computation).
- Implementing collective overlap with loop-carried futures is complicated by the fact that many of the async utils assume that each done has a unique start, which is not the case with loop-carried futures (we have one start before the loop body, and one inside the body from the previous iteration). Support for loop-carried futures will be improved in follow-up PRs; this PR fixes cases where an async start and done are in the same computation.
- Several LHS functions other than `GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit` (e.g. `CanonicalAsyncStart`, `IsAnnotatedForGpuAsyncStreamCollectivesP2P`, `IsCollectivesGroupAsyncDoneOp`) also assume that the done's first operand is the start. Follow-up PRs will address those functions.

🎯 Justification

Without this fix, when collective multi-streaming is enabled or the module uses multiple collective communication domains, an async collective whose async-done does not consume its async-start directly is never allowed to overlap another in-flight collective. This needlessly serializes collectives, and when data dependencies force the overlap, the LHS fails to schedule valid HLO. `OverlapLimitResolvesAsyncStartThroughIntermediaries` demonstrates the failing case.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `gpu_latency_hiding_scheduler_test.cc`:

- `OverlapLimitResolvesAsyncStartThroughIntermediaries`: schedules HLO with two async all-gathers whose starts and dones are separated by an `opt-barrier`. Both must be in flight at the same time and each `async-done` reaches its `async-start` through `tuple`, `opt-barrier`, and `get-tuple-element`. The two all-gathers share at most one device, so this is allowed. Without this PR's change, scheduling fails with `FindAndExtractBestNodeAvailable failed to find a node to schedule`.
- `OverlapLimitRejectsLoopCarriedAsyncDoneWithUnknownStart`: schedules HLO with a pipelined all-gather whose start is carried into the while body from the previous iteration. `opt-barrier`s force another all-gather to be in flight when the carried `async-done` is scheduled, and since the start is not in the same computation as the done, the scheduler conservatively refuses to overlap them even though they share at most one device.

display_title: [XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject overflowing dimensions in Array and Mesh::FromProto

`Array` computed its element count with an unchecked signed product, so
dimensions such as {3, 6148914691236517206} wrapped around to a small
allocation while the dimensions still described a huge array. A `MeshProto`
with such axis sizes and matching `device_ids` produced a `Mesh` whose later
transposes, indexing and tile iteration read and wrote out of bounds.

`Array` now CHECK-fails on negative dimensions and on overflow of the product
of its nonzero dimensions, both on construction and in `Reshape`.
`Mesh::FromProto` additionally checks the axis-size product for overflow and
validates the number of device ids before allocating the device id array.

head_commit.message:
PR #53101: [ROCm] Non-temporal cache hints for gfx942

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53101

📝 Summary of Changes
On MI300, MLIR kernels mark large streamed loads and stores non-temporal. Loads need a buffer of at least 16×L2 (64 MiB) that is read once; stores need one qualifying output in a contiguous kernel.

🎯 Justification
Data touched once otherwise evicts reused data from L2 and from MI300X's Infinity Cache. This helps memory-bound fusions over large buffers.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: ⚡️ Performance Improvement, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Synthetic streaming kernels of 64–512 MiB average −11.5%.

🧪 Unit Tests:
nontemporal_hints_test.cc,  lower_tensors_amdgpu_nontemporal.mlir, mlir_kernel_emitter_test.cc

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Cache symmetric memory registrations on communicators.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cache symmetric memory registrations on communicators.

Previously, `CollectiveMemoryCache` was owned per `GpuExecutable` and keyed by the exact sub-allocation address, preventing symmetric memory windows from being reused across executables sharing a communicator or across sub-slices of the same physical collective arena.
This change moves registration ownership to the GPU communicator instead. Instead of registering one specific buffer allocation, this change queries `StreamExecutor::GetMemoryRange` in `AcquireCollectiveMemory` to register the enclosing physical memory. This works since collective memory space should be symmetrical across all participant devices and it should be allocated from the beginning of the physically allocated arena.

display_title: Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

head_commit.message:
Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. With the HloModule stored in the base class, every executable
had to carry one to answer metadata queries.

Move `hlo_module_` and `module_stats_` and the implementations that read them
into `HloModuleExecutable`:

- `shared_module()` (nullable), `module_config()`, `result_shape()`,
  `compute_computation_layout()`, `name()`, `input_output_alias_config()`,
  `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()` are pure virtual on
  `Executable`. `set_module_stats()` lives on `HloModuleExecutable`.
- `module()` and `has_module()` stay as non-virtual helpers on top of a new
  protected pure virtual `module_ptr()`, so they don't copy a
  `std::shared_ptr`.
- Virtuals that don't need state keep their defaults
  (`SizeOfGeneratedCodeInBytes()`, `GetAllocations()`, ...).
- The unused `execution_count_` is deleted.

The only state left in `Executable` is the HLO proto for debugging
(`hlo_proto_` and its mutex). It still fills in the module lazily through
`module()`. Later changes move its producers and readers away and remove it.

`HloModuleExecutable` implements everything from the module as before, so
there is no behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that
derive from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable`
instead (or implement the new pure virtuals).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use LaunchDimensions for CTA cluster dimensions in GPU runtime

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use LaunchDimensions for CTA cluster dimensions in GPU runtime

`KernelThunk`, `ExecuteKernelOnStream`, `KernelThunkToString`, and
`FfiLaunchParams` still handled `se::ClusterDim` separately from
`LaunchDimensions`, while `CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()` dropped
`custom_kernel_.cluster_dims()`.

Read CTA cluster dimensions directly from `LaunchDimensions::cluster_dims()`
across GPU runtime thunks and stream launch helpers, and preserve them in
`CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()`.

To preserve 2-week forward compatibility, `KernelThunk::ToProto()` dual-writes
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` alongside `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims`.
For 6-month backward compatibility, `KernelThunk::FromProto()` falls back to
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` when `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims` is
unset.

display_title: PR #53038: Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively for non-ASCII paths

head_commit.message:
PR #53038: Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively for non-ASCII paths

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53038

#ai-generated

**Status quo**
`WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory` and `WindowsFileSystem::DeleteRecursively` convert the wide-character path back to `std::string` by range-constructing it from the `std::wstring`, which keeps only the low byte of each wide character. Any path segment above U+007F — a user folder like 王小明 or café — is mangled, so `IsDirectory` fails on directories that exist and `DeleteRecursively` works on a wrong name. In TensorFlow this breaks the flows built on these calls (`isdir`, `makedirs`, `saved_model.save`, `CheckpointManager.save`) for non-ASCII directory names on Windows. Real users hit this in tensorflow/tensorflow#62691 and tensorflow/tensorflow#61550; both were closed as stale without a fix.

**Why**
Non-ASCII user and folder names are the default outside English locales, and saving a model or a checkpoint into such a folder is a basic flow, not an edge case. The reports were closed for staleness, not because the bug went away.

**Design**
Convert with the existing `WideCharToUtf8()` helper instead of the truncating range constructor, in both places (two lines). No other call sites change.

**Testing**
New `EnvTest.NonAsciiDirectoryNames` in `xla/tsl/platform/env_test.cc`: creates `café/王`, checks `RecursivelyCreateDir`, `IsDirectory` on both levels, writes a file, then `DeleteRecursively` and confirms the tree is gone. Reproduced with TensorFlow 2.21.0: the two changed functions return NotFound before and OK after.

One honest limitation: XLA's GitHub CI has no Windows job, so this test's Windows coverage only runs downstream (e.g. TensorFlow's Windows builds). On Linux the test passes either way, since UTF-8 paths are native there.

c6195d503f8dfa91cd36f62366bdcb9980876599 by b84330808 <b84330808@gmail.com>:

[XLA/TSL] Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory for non-ASCII paths

IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively turned the wide UNC path back into a
std::string by narrowing each wchar_t to a char. For any non-ASCII
character that drops the high byte (U+00E9 becomes 0xE9, U+738B becomes
0x8B), so the FileExists() call that follows looks up a different, invalid
UTF-8 name and fails. Convert with WideCharToUtf8() instead, as the rest of
the file does.

On Windows this made IsDirectory fail for every directory whose path
contains a non-ASCII character, which breaks RecursivelyCreateDir under
such a directory, GetMatchingPaths patterns that recurse into it, Stat's
is_directory, and DeleteRecursively.

Merging this change closes #53038

display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

display_title: [XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

📝 Summary of Changes

PR #52906 restricted HandleMaximum's maximum(a, clamp(a, x, b)) -> clamp(a, x, b) rewrite using IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (via HloEvaluator and ComparisonDirection::kLe).
That still leaves several issues:
- +0.0 <= -0.0 evaluates to true under partial order, folding max(+0.0, clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0)) to clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0) (-0.0 instead of +0.0).
- Building a kLt/kLe kCompare and calling HloEvaluator::Evaluate aborts AlgebraicSimplifier::Run() with UnimplementedError on complex bounds (c64/c128) and TF_RET_CHECK-fails on mixed-FP bounds (both in HandleMaximum and in MinMaxToClamp).
- IsKnownLessThanOrEqual folds lhs == rhs unconditionally and allocates a fresh HloEvaluator on every match.

This change replaces IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (and HloEvaluator in MinMaxToClamp) with a shared CompareConstantBounds helper that checks matching, non-complex array element types and evaluates strict lower < upper directly on the scalar literals via PrimitiveTypeSwitch and Comparison, removing the hlo_evaluator dependency from algebraic_simplifier. Degenerate equal-bound clamps (a == b) are not worth special-casing, matching MinMaxToClamp.

🎯 Justification

Follow-up to #52659 / #52906: prevents sign-bit flips on (+0.0, -0.0) clamp bounds, prevents AlgebraicSimplifier pass failures on complex or mixed-precision bounds, and avoids HloEvaluator overhead during simplification.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc:
- MaxOfClamp: ordered constant bounds (0 and 6); expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithBroadcastBounds: broadcast ordered bounds with maximum operands swapped; expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithUnorderedBounds: constant bounds 10 and 0; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithParameterBounds: runtime parameter bounds; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithSignedZeroBounds: constant bounds +0.0 and -0.0; expects no change (fails with a <= check).
- MaxOfClampWithComplexBounds: c64 constant bounds; expects no change without failing.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

display_title: PR #53387: [XLA:GPU] Resolve async-start through async intermediaries in LHS GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit

head_commit.message:
PR #53387: [XLA:GPU] Resolve async-start through async intermediaries in LHS GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53387

📝 Summary of Changes

`GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit` was assuming that the async-start corresponding to a candidate async-done is always the done's first operand. This is not the case when the start reaches the done through intermediary instructions (e.g. `tuple`, `opt-barrier`, `get-tuple-element`, etc). This PR uses the `FindStart()` helper to resolve the async-start through intermediaries. If `FindStart` cannot resolve a start in the computation being scheduled, the function conservatively reports that the overlap limit is crossed.

Limitations:
- Overlapping a collective with a loop-carried future is unsupported. This is because `FindStart()` only returns an async-start if the start is in the same computation as the done, which isn't the case with while ops (the done in the body has a start reachable from the caller computation).
- Implementing collective overlap with loop-carried futures is complicated by the fact that many of the async utils assume that each done has a unique start, which is not the case with loop-carried futures (we have one start before the loop body, and one inside the body from the previous iteration). Support for loop-carried futures will be improved in follow-up PRs; this PR fixes cases where an async start and done are in the same computation.
- Several LHS functions other than `GpuScheduleCrossesOverlapLimit` (e.g. `CanonicalAsyncStart`, `IsAnnotatedForGpuAsyncStreamCollectivesP2P`, `IsCollectivesGroupAsyncDoneOp`) also assume that the done's first operand is the start. Follow-up PRs will address those functions.

🎯 Justification

Without this fix, when collective multi-streaming is enabled or the module uses multiple collective communication domains, an async collective whose async-done does not consume its async-start directly is never allowed to overlap another in-flight collective. This needlessly serializes collectives, and when data dependencies force the overlap, the LHS fails to schedule valid HLO. `OverlapLimitResolvesAsyncStartThroughIntermediaries` demonstrates the failing case.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `gpu_latency_hiding_scheduler_test.cc`:

- `OverlapLimitResolvesAsyncStartThroughIntermediaries`: schedules HLO with two async all-gathers whose starts and dones are separated by an `opt-barrier`. Both must be in flight at the same time and each `async-done` reaches its `async-start` through `tuple`, `opt-barrier`, and `get-tuple-element`. The two all-gathers share at most one device, so this is allowed. Without this PR's change, scheduling fails with `FindAndExtractBestNodeAvailable failed to find a node to schedule`.
- `OverlapLimitRejectsLoopCarriedAsyncDoneWithUnknownStart`: schedules HLO with a pipelined all-gather whose start is carried into the while body from the previous iteration. `opt-barrier`s force another all-gather to be in flight when the carried `async-done` is scheduled, and since the start is not in the same computation as the done, the scheduler conservatively refuses to overlap them even though they share at most one device.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use A100 instead of V100 in cuDNN deviceless fusion tests.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use A100 instead of V100 in cuDNN deviceless fusion tests.

cuDNN 9.11 dropped execution support for compute capability below 7.5 (Volta and older). cuDNN Frontend v1.33.0 now declines SM70 targets up front in `create_execution_plans` and `check_support`. Because `CudnnFusionCompilerDevicelessTest` requires cuDNN 9.15 or newer, probing `GpuModel::V100` (sm_70) now returns `kUnsupported` for plain f32 convolutions. That SM floor also masks the FP8 check in `Fp8ConvVerdictTracksTargetGpu`.

Switch `PlainF32ConvAllKindsSupported` and `Fp8ConvVerdictTracksTargetGpu` from `GpuModel::V100` to `GpuModel::A100_SXM_80` (sm_80). cuDNN 9.11 and newer support sm_80 for f32 convolutions while still rejecting FP8 convolutions, which require sm_89 or newer.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

`RecordKernelLaunch` unconditionally prepended `ctx->dependencies` even when a handler passed explicit `dependencies`. In a multi-command `Record` handler, chained launches got redundant direct edges from preceding thunks (and spurious programmatic edges when `uses_pdl` was set). Conversely, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D` and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand` ignored `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, leaving root memcpy and empty commands without edges from preceding thunks, and skipped null checks on `ctx`, `out_command`, and `dependencies`.

Share a single `ResolveDependencies` helper across `RecordKernelLaunch`, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D`, and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand`: inherit `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, and validate and forward only the caller-specified commands when `num_dependencies > 0`.

display_title: Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

head_commit.message:
Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. `hlo_proto_` on the base mixes up two things: the buffer assignment
that the backend owns, and an HLO snapshot that the creator attaches for
dumping. This CL starts to pull them apart.

`Executable::buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes virtual. The default still
reads `hlo_proto_`. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` override it from state
they own, and return it in exactly the cases where the base accessor returns
non-null today:

- `GpuExecutable` returns its buffer assignment proto only if the compiler
  embeds debug info and keeps the HloModule
  (`Params::expose_buffer_assignment_proto`). Executables loaded from a proto
  still return nullptr. The always-available GPU accessor is renamed to
  `owned_buffer_assignment_proto()`, because a non-virtual accessor with the
  same name would hide the virtual one.
- `CpuExecutable` gets an optional buffer assignment proto that the CPU
  compiler sets with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, and the CPU AOT loader with
  `xla_embed_ir_in_executable` or `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots`.

The compilers still call `set_hlo_proto`; that goes away in a follow-up.

No behaviour change.

display_title: Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

head_commit.message:
Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The HLO that goes into HLO snapshots is debug state of whoever runs
the executable, so it moves out of `Executable::hlo_proto_`:

- `Service::BuildExecutable` returns the HLO before optimizations (plus the
  buffer assignment after optimizations) through an optional out-param instead
  of `set_hlo_proto`. `Service::Compile` keeps it in the `CompilationCache`
  entry, and `Service::Execute` reads it from there.
- `LocalExecutable` gets an optional snapshot HLO, filled through a new
  optional out-param of `LocalService::CompileExecutables`. Executables loaded
  with `LocalClient::Load` don't have one.
- New free helpers in `xla/service/executable.h`: `DumpingHloSnapshots()`
  replaces `Executable::dumping_snapshot()` at these call sites, and
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()` builds the snapshot HLO from the executable's
  HloModule and buffer assignment if nobody kept one.
- The HLO before optimizations is only built if `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots` is
  set, since snapshots are its only reader.
- The CPU AOT loader no longer attaches a full HloProto when dumping snapshots;
  the fallback above produces the same content.
- Deletes the unused `HloRunnerLegacy::HloProtoFromWrapped`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Order producer-consumer adaptor instructions like the fused fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Order producer-consumer adaptor instructions like the fused fusion

`HloFusionAdaptor::MakeInstructionPostOrder()` returned the producer's
instructions followed by the consumer's. The fused computation visits the
producer where the consumer first reads it, after the consumer instructions
that come before that operand. The two orders differ for
`add(reduce(a), producer)`.

Instead, the adaptor now inserts the producer's instructions where the consumer first reads the producer.

This is needed for correctness because the config for sequential dimensions relies on the positional information.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over a dimension that is not logically last.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over a dimension that is not logically last.

Triton scans had two requirements on the scan dimension: `CanTritonHandleScan` required it to be the last logical dimension, and `ScanRewriterTriton` requires it to be physically last, i.e. minor-most in the layout. Remove the logical requirement. The physical one stays, because Triton scans over other dimensions are generally less efficient.

The logical requirement worked around a wrong launch grid. A Triton scan fusion processes the whole scan dimension inside each block, so its output tile sizes have no entry for that dimension. `TritonFusion::GetLaunchConfig` matched the tile sizes with the leading dimensions of the fusion root, which gives the right number of blocks only when the scan dimension is logically last.

Skip the scan dimensions when counting tiles. They are found by walking from the fusion roots through get-tuple-element and elementwise ops, as `TilingSpace` does.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix dependency resolution in FFI Record command creation.

`RecordKernelLaunch` unconditionally prepended `ctx->dependencies` even when a handler passed explicit `dependencies`. In a multi-command `Record` handler, chained launches got redundant direct edges from preceding thunks (and spurious programmatic edges when `uses_pdl` was set). Conversely, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D` and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand` ignored `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, leaving root memcpy and empty commands without edges from preceding thunks, and skipped null checks on `ctx`, `out_command`, and `dependencies`.

Share a single `ResolveDependencies` helper across `RecordKernelLaunch`, `FfiCreateMemcpyD2D`, and `FfiCreateEmptyCommand`: inherit `ctx->dependencies` when `num_dependencies == 0`, and validate and forward only the caller-specified commands when `num_dependencies > 0`.

display_title: Fix BufferFromHostLiteral lifetime bugs in PJRT tests

head_commit.message:
Fix BufferFromHostLiteral lifetime bugs in PJRT tests

`BufferFromHostLiteral` requires the caller to keep `literal` alive until the
asynchronous host-to-device copy completes, which two StreamExecutor PJRT
error-path tests violate:

- `CrossHostTransferPoisonedDescriptor` in
  `xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_pjrt_cross_host_transfer_test.cc` aborts
  `ScheduleRemoteSend` before awaiting the transfer, so test teardown frees
  `input_literal` while `client`'s background worker is still reading it.
- `CrossClientCopyToMemorySpacePropagatesAllocatorFailure` in
  `xla/pjrt/se/pjrt_stream_executor_client_test.cc` passes a temporary
  `Literal` prvalue to `BufferFromHostLiteral`, freeing the host buffer before
  the asynchronous `Memcpy` runs.

Since neither test inspects buffer contents, let's use
`CreateUninitializedBuffer` instead so no host `Literal` or host-to-device
transfer is scheduled.

display_title: PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

head_commit.message:
PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52875

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

display_title: [NFC] Move `HloValue` state from `BufferAllocation` to `BufferAssignment`

head_commit.message:
[NFC] Move `HloValue` state from `BufferAllocation` to `BufferAssignment`

`BufferAllocation` is used by runtime targets that only need allocation metadata and slices, so it shouldn't depend on `HloValue` (which pulls in `hlo/ir:hlo`).

We move the per-allocation `HloValue` state and heap traces into a parallel `allocation_values_` vector in `BufferAssignment` (indexed by `BufferAllocation::index()`) and remove the `HloValue` accessors from `BufferAllocation`.

We keep serializing `assigned` inside `BufferAllocationProto` (populated by `BufferAssignment::ToProto()`, while standalone `BufferAllocation::ToProto()` leaves it empty) rather than moving it onto `BufferAssignmentProto` for now. Several `HloProto` consumers (e.g. XProf and `ComputePeakMemorySizes`) read `BufferAllocationProto.assigned` directly instead of going through `BufferAssignment::FromProto()`. Switching the writer right away would also break CPU/GPU AOT forward compatibility when older readers load new protos, so moving the proto field would require a multi-stage rollout across repos.

A follow up CL will actually split the files

display_title: [XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

📝 Summary of Changes

PR #52906 restricted HandleMaximum's maximum(a, clamp(a, x, b)) -> clamp(a, x, b) rewrite using IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (via HloEvaluator and ComparisonDirection::kLe).
That still leaves several issues:
- +0.0 <= -0.0 evaluates to true under partial order, folding max(+0.0, clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0)) to clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0) (-0.0 instead of +0.0).
- Building a kLt/kLe kCompare and calling HloEvaluator::Evaluate aborts AlgebraicSimplifier::Run() with UnimplementedError on complex bounds (c64/c128) and TF_RET_CHECK-fails on mixed-FP bounds (both in HandleMaximum and in MinMaxToClamp).
- IsKnownLessThanOrEqual folds lhs == rhs unconditionally and allocates a fresh HloEvaluator on every match.

This change replaces IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (and HloEvaluator in MinMaxToClamp) with a shared CompareConstantBounds helper that checks matching, non-complex array element types and evaluates strict lower < upper directly on the scalar literals via PrimitiveTypeSwitch and Comparison, removing the hlo_evaluator dependency from algebraic_simplifier. Degenerate equal-bound clamps (a == b) are not worth special-casing, matching MinMaxToClamp.

🎯 Justification

Follow-up to #52659 / #52906: prevents sign-bit flips on (+0.0, -0.0) clamp bounds, prevents AlgebraicSimplifier pass failures on complex or mixed-precision bounds, and avoids HloEvaluator overhead during simplification.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc:
- MaxOfClamp: ordered constant bounds (0 and 6); expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithBroadcastBounds: broadcast ordered bounds with maximum operands swapped; expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithUnorderedBounds: constant bounds 10 and 0; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithParameterBounds: runtime parameter bounds; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithSignedZeroBounds: constant bounds +0.0 and -0.0; expects no change (fails with a <= check).
- MaxOfClampWithComplexBounds: c64 constant bounds; expects no change without failing.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

display_title: Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

head_commit.message:
Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. With the HloModule stored in the base class, every executable
had to carry one to answer metadata queries.

Move `hlo_module_` and `module_stats_` and the implementations that read them
into `HloModuleExecutable`:

- `shared_module()` (nullable), `module_config()`, `result_shape()`,
  `compute_computation_layout()`, `name()`, `input_output_alias_config()`,
  `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()` are pure virtual on
  `Executable`. `set_module_stats()` lives on `HloModuleExecutable`.
- `module()` and `has_module()` stay as non-virtual helpers on top of a new
  protected pure virtual `module_ptr()`, so they don't copy a
  `std::shared_ptr`.
- Virtuals that don't need state keep their defaults
  (`SizeOfGeneratedCodeInBytes()`, `GetAllocations()`, ...).
- The unused `execution_count_` is deleted.

The only state left in `Executable` is the HLO proto for debugging
(`hlo_proto_` and its mutex). It still fills in the module lazily through
`module()`. Later changes move its producers and readers away and remove it.

`HloModuleExecutable` implements everything from the module as before, so
there is no behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that
derive from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable`
instead (or implement the new pure virtuals).
