head_commit.message:
[XLA] Only fold max(a, clamp(a, x, b)) into the clamp when a < b

📝 Summary of Changes

PR #52906 restricted HandleMaximum's maximum(a, clamp(a, x, b)) -> clamp(a, x, b) rewrite using IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (via HloEvaluator and ComparisonDirection::kLe).
That still leaves several issues:
- +0.0 <= -0.0 evaluates to true under partial order, folding max(+0.0, clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0)) to clamp(+0.0, x, -0.0) (-0.0 instead of +0.0).
- Building a kLt/kLe kCompare and calling HloEvaluator::Evaluate aborts AlgebraicSimplifier::Run() with UnimplementedError on complex bounds (c64/c128) and TF_RET_CHECK-fails on mixed-FP bounds (both in HandleMaximum and in MinMaxToClamp).
- IsKnownLessThanOrEqual folds lhs == rhs unconditionally and allocates a fresh HloEvaluator on every match.

This change replaces IsKnownLessThanOrEqual (and HloEvaluator in MinMaxToClamp) with a shared CompareConstantBounds helper that checks matching, non-complex array element types and evaluates strict lower < upper directly on the scalar literals via PrimitiveTypeSwitch and Comparison, removing the hlo_evaluator dependency from algebraic_simplifier. Degenerate equal-bound clamps (a == b) are not worth special-casing, matching MinMaxToClamp.

🎯 Justification

Follow-up to #52659 / #52906: prevents sign-bit flips on (+0.0, -0.0) clamp bounds, prevents AlgebraicSimplifier pass failures on complex or mixed-precision bounds, and avoids HloEvaluator overhead during simplification.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier_test.cc:
- MaxOfClamp: ordered constant bounds (0 and 6); expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithBroadcastBounds: broadcast ordered bounds with maximum operands swapped; expects the fold.
- MaxOfClampWithUnorderedBounds: constant bounds 10 and 0; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithParameterBounds: runtime parameter bounds; expects no change.
- MaxOfClampWithSignedZeroBounds: constant bounds +0.0 and -0.0; expects no change (fails with a <= check).
- MaxOfClampWithComplexBounds: c64 constant bounds; expects no change without failing.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added.

head_commit.message:
Use CreateUninitializedBuffer in GPU external DMA tests

Four `AcquireExternalDmaAccess` tests in
`xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_pjrt_client_test.cc` allocate buffers from a stack-local
`Literal` via `BufferFromHostLiteral` without waiting for the asynchronous
host-to-device copy to finish. `AcquireExternalDmaAccess` only waits for buffer
allocation (or returns an error immediately on host memory or when `dma-buf`
export is unsupported, such as on ROCm). Because `client` outlives `literal` on
the stack, destroying `literal` on test exit races with the background
linearization worker and triggers an ASan heap-use-after-free.

Since none of these tests inspect buffer contents, let's use
`CreateUninitializedBuffer` instead (matching
`AcquireExternalDmaAccessKeepsBufferAlive`). This way we avoid allocating a host
`Literal` or scheduling a host-to-device transfer altogether across all four
tests (extending https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53655).

head_commit.message:
[NFC] Move `HloValue` state from `BufferAllocation` to `BufferAssignment`

`BufferAllocation` is used by runtime targets that only need allocation metadata and slices, so it shouldn't depend on `HloValue` (which pulls in `hlo/ir:hlo`).

We move the per-allocation `HloValue` state and heap traces into a parallel `allocation_values_` vector in `BufferAssignment` (indexed by `BufferAllocation::index()`) and remove the `HloValue` accessors from `BufferAllocation`.

We keep serializing `assigned` inside `BufferAllocationProto` (populated by `BufferAssignment::ToProto()`, while standalone `BufferAllocation::ToProto()` leaves it empty) rather than moving it onto `BufferAssignmentProto` for now. Several `HloProto` consumers (e.g. XProf and `ComputePeakMemorySizes`) read `BufferAllocationProto.assigned` directly instead of going through `BufferAssignment::FromProto()`. Switching the writer right away would also break CPU/GPU AOT forward compatibility when older readers load new protos, so moving the proto field would require a multi-stage rollout across repos.

head_commit.message:
PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52875

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

Copybara import of the project:

display_title: Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

head_commit.message:
Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

`LowerTensorsPass` currently mixes shared tensor-to-LLVM lowering with GPU
dialect ops, device capabilities, and vendor-specific atomics in one target,
forcing XLA:CPU to pull in GPU dependencies. Our end goal is to replace the
unified `LowerTensorsPass` with separate CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes. As
the first step, separate the target-neutral core from the GPU patterns without
changing end-to-end CPU or GPU codegen.

Move the shared two-phase driver and target-neutral tensor and atomic patterns
into `lower_tensors_common` (`LowerTensors` and `LowerTensorsConfig`) with no
GPU dependencies. Trace pass-through destination buffers via
`mlir::DestinationStyleOpInterface` on `xla` and `xla_gpu` ops, and mark
`xla_gpu.allocate_shared` with `MemAlloc`.

Move GPU-specific patterns (`allocate_shared`, `sync_threads`, sub-byte
mid-word `set_dynamic_dim_size`, and NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel direct atomics)
into `LowerGpuTensors` under `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/`.
Pre-lower `allocate_shared` before the main tensor patterns so buffer alignment
derives directly from `llvm.mlir.global`. Keep `LowerTensorsPass` as a
temporary thin wrapper that skips GPU patterns on CPU, and restrict `xla_gpu`
checks in `lower_tensors.mlir` to `CHECK-GPU`.

The next step will add dedicated CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes in their
respective backend packages, migrate callers and tests, and remove
`LowerTensorsPass` from `//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms:passes`. That step
will drop the following GPU dependencies from XLA:CPU:
- `//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms:lower_tensors_patterns`
- `@llvm-project//mlir:ROCDLDialect`
- `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_compute_capability`
- `//xla/stream_executor/rocm:rocm_compute_capability`

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model occupancy for reduction fusion estimates

We are reusing the occupancy function in the dot cost model as it doesn't have operation specific logic and can be used here.

`GpuPerformanceModelWithIndexingAnalysis` assumes that the compute and memory
access time of a tiled fusion overlap almost fully, whatever the tile size.
Blocks are not pipelined, so the compute of a block only overlaps with the
memory accesses of the other blocks resident on the same core.

We should expand the occupancy measure beyond reductions. I only have evidence that it helps reductions, and generalizing this needs to be validated first. I'd rather do this incrementally.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over a dimension that is not logically last.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over a dimension that is not logically last.

Triton scans had two requirements on the scan dimension: `CanTritonHandleScan` required it to be the last logical dimension, and `ScanRewriterTriton` requires it to be physically last, i.e. minor-most in the layout. Remove the logical requirement. The physical one stays, because Triton scans over other dimensions are generally less efficient.

The logical requirement worked around a wrong launch grid. A Triton scan fusion processes the whole scan dimension inside each block, so its output tile sizes have no entry for that dimension. `TritonFusion::GetLaunchConfig` matched the tile sizes with the leading dimensions of the fusion root, which gives the right number of blocks only when the scan dimension is logically last.

Skip the scan dimensions when counting tiles. They are found by walking from the fusion roots through get-tuple-element and elementwise ops, as `TilingSpace` does.

display_title: Use CreateUninitializedBuffer in GPU external DMA tests

head_commit.message:
Use CreateUninitializedBuffer in GPU external DMA tests

Four `AcquireExternalDmaAccess` tests in
`xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_pjrt_client_test.cc` allocate buffers from a stack-local
`Literal` via `BufferFromHostLiteral` without waiting for the asynchronous
host-to-device copy to finish. `AcquireExternalDmaAccess` only waits for buffer
allocation (or returns an error immediately on host memory or when `dma-buf`
export is unsupported, such as on ROCm). Because `client` outlives `literal` on
the stack, destroying `literal` on test exit races with the background
linearization worker and triggers an ASan heap-use-after-free.

Since none of these tests inspect buffer contents, let's use
`CreateUninitializedBuffer` instead (matching
`AcquireExternalDmaAccessKeepsBufferAlive`). This way we avoid allocating a host
`Literal` or scheduling a host-to-device transfer altogether across all four
tests (extending https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53655).

display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Model occupancy for reduction fusion estimates

We are reusing the occupancy function in the dot cost model as it doesn't have operation specific logic and can be used here.

`GpuPerformanceModelWithIndexingAnalysis` assumes that the compute and memory
access time of a tiled fusion overlap almost fully, whatever the tile size.
Blocks are not pipelined, so the compute of a block only overlaps with the
memory accesses of the other blocks resident on the same core.

We should expand the occupancy measure beyond reductions. I only have evidence that it helps reductions, and generalizing this needs to be validated first. I'd rather do this incrementally.

display_title: PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

head_commit.message:
PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52875

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

Copybara import of the project:

--
31a033f4fa91d10341fdf72912cb598e76a438e7 by Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>:

[XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Keep oneDNN fusion outputs separate from their inputs because the
compiled partition's in-place requirements are unavailable during
buffer assignment. This prevents fused matmul from overwriting the
zero operand before maximum applies ReLU.

Add allocation and execution regressions while preserving buffer reuse
for ordinary loop fusions.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>

--
a5ff64ae155c8f93a879135eefae6eaff7bb042a by Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>:

[XLA:CPU] Preserve safe custom fusion buffer reuse

Deny inferred buffer reuse for custom fusions unless their runtime
supports it. Preserve YNNPACK's existing HLO sharing rules and share
CpuAliasInfo between compilation and AOT loading.

Cover aliased oneDNN inputs through copy insertion and execution, plus
YNNPACK reuse. Keep the regression enabled on AArch64.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>

--
29013e26e909611beea3b14cda516430d7236fe4 by Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>:

[XLA:CPU] Fix fusion test CI checks

Add the headers and Bazel dependencies used by the fusion regressions.
Teach DWYU to recognize dependencies inside if_onednn, and cover the
missing-dependency false positive.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>

--
a8c5991f4c0e95f2968faeb94847e0da7e361ce8 by Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>:

[XLA:CPU] Indent the oneDNN dependency test fixture

Use textwrap.dedent to keep the embedded BUILD text indented within the
regression test while preserving the generated file contents.

Signed-off-by: Pablo Marquez Tello <pablo.tello@arm.com>

Merging this change closes #52875

head_commit.message:
PR #53581: [XLA:GPU][SPIR-V] Use legacy bf16 arithmetic SPIR-V extension name

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53581

This PR reverts https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/c98da0aa080528159113ff0558a0b334d2c61d1e
That commit switched the SPIR-V backend to use `SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic` to fix the oneAPI build after LLVM dropped `SPV_INTEL_bfloat16_arithmetic`.

https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/74d28467487ad6559462889107748a8e1ea8b488 restored `SPV_INTEL_bfloat16_arithmetic` as a legacy alias. It enables the same capability and generates SPIR-V with the same semantics. This PR replaces `SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic` with `SPV_INTEL_bfloat16_arithmetic` in the extension set so the backend emits the name that legacy drivers accept.
We can switch back to `SPV_EXT_bfloat16_arithmetic` once the minimum supported driver recognizes it.

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

📝 Summary of Changes
Wait for H2D transfer in AcquireExternalDmaAccessSlicedBuffer test

StreamExecutorGpuClientTest.AcquireExternalDmaAccessSlicedBuffer fails under ASan on ROCm with a heap-use-after-free. head_commit.message:
Re-enable Triton amd-range-analysis lit test and fix overflow patch

The upstream Triton fix (commit 6559dea9d66c20590b4a7aa0cafa850b55269a1e) for
`amd-range-analysis.mlir` has landed, so the test exclusion is no longer needed.
Re-enabling the test exposed a regression in `amd_range_analysis.patch`.
`getTotalLoopTripCount()` clamped trip counts to `kDefaultMaxTripCount + 1`
(1025) instead of only guarding against signed 64-bit overflow.

Use `llvm::MulOverflow` in `getTotalLoopTripCount()` so non-overflowing trip
counts remain exact while overflows fall back to `kDefaultMaxTripCount + 1`.
Remove the test exclusion and regenerate the Triton patch files.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53581

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Destroy acquired GPU cliques in GpuExecutableTest

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Destroy acquired GPU cliques in GpuExecutableTest

`RendezvousAfterExecutionPreventsDriverLockDeadlockAcrossExecutables` acquires a `GpuClique` with stack-allocated `se::MockStreamExecutor` instances and never clears process-global cliques on exit. When `BFCAllocator` tears down in a later test, `gpu::ReleaseSymmetricMemory` iterates cached cliques and dereferences the destroyed `MockStreamExecutor` pointer, causing `SIGSEGV`.

Under `--gtest_shuffle`, this crashes whenever `ExecuteWithWatchdogs` runs after the rendezvous test (~50% failure rate on single-attempt ROCm CI and ~12.5% on 3-attempt T4 CI). Add an `absl::Cleanup` guard calling `internal::DestroyAcquiredCliques()` before `executors` and `loopback_collectives` leave scope.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1027922195

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Destroy acquired GPU cliques in GpuExecutableTest

`RendezvousAfterExecutionPreventsDriverLockDeadlockAcrossExecutables` acquires a `GpuClique` with stack-allocated `se::MockStreamExecutor` instances and never clears process-global cliques on exit. When `BFCAllocator` tears down in a later test, `gpu::ReleaseSymmetricMemory` iterates cached cliques and dereferences the destroyed `MockStreamExecutor` pointer, causing `SIGSEGV`.

Under `--gtest_shuffle`, this crashes whenever `ExecuteWithWatchdogs` runs after the rendezvous test (~50% failure rate on single-attempt ROCm CI and ~12.5% on 3-attempt T4 CI). Add an `absl::Cleanup` guard calling `internal::DestroyAcquiredCliques()` before `executors` and `loopback_collectives` leave scope.

display_title: Add 6-bit BitPlaneProto strip linearization in TiledLinearizer.

head_commit.message:
Add 6-bit BitPlaneProto strip linearization in TiledLinearizer.

`TiledLinearizer` previously rejected all `BitPlaneProto` layouts with `UnimplementedError`, blocking host-to-device linearization and device-to-host delinearization for 6-bit floating-point TPU tensors.

Support 128-lane 6-bit `BP(4:...)(2:...)` split strip layouts (`{1,0:T(T_0,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}`, `{1,0:T(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}`, and 0D/1D `{...T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}`) in `TiledLinearizer` using Highway SIMD strip repack helpers (`Repack6BitStripToHardwareLayoutHighway` and `Repack6BitStripToHostLayoutHighway`) that pack 1-byte host strips into 3-sublane interleaved 4-bit/2-bit hardware strips and unpack them back to host layout, with checked 64-bit tile and strip size arithmetic.

Verified 0D/1D/2D/3D 6-bit `BP(...)` `TiledLinearizer` round-trips, unaligned 1D host buffers, dynamic metadata prefixes, non-contiguous host strides, partial strips, `set_padding_to_nan`, and element-type/layout/strip-size/overflow validation in unit tests.

Assign default 6-bit BitPlaneProto split layouts for FP6 and bump ABI.

display_title: Add BitPlaneProto layout representation.

head_commit.message:
Add BitPlaneProto layout representation.

6-bit floating-point TPU layouts split each `(16, 128)` strip across non-adjacent 4-bit and 2-bit sublanes, whereas `LayoutProto.element_size_in_bits` (`E(n)`) specifies contiguous `n`-bit elements. Overloading `E(6)` broke contiguous `E(n)` semantics and layout size queries.

Add `BitPlaneProto` (`bit_planes` in `LayoutProto`, printed as `BP(w[:tiles])` or `BP(w@offset[:tiles])`) supporting both per-strip splits with outer `tiles` (such as `{1,0:T(256,128)(16,128)BP(4:(8,1))(2:(16,1))}` and `{0:T(2048)BP(4:(128)(8,1))(2:(128)(16,1))}`) and whole-tensor splits with empty outer `tiles` (such as 64-bit integer `{1,0:BP(32:(8,128))(32:(8,128))}`), while keeping `sizeof(xla::Layout)` unchanged. Update `LayoutUtil`, `ShapeUtil`, `HloParser`, `LayoutAssignment`, HLO simplifiers, and Python `xc.Layout`, and guard unsupported CPU/GPU, generic PJRT, `TiledLinearizer`, and C API paths.

Verified `BitPlaneProto` parsing, contiguous bit-plane validation, `LogicalBitWidth`, `ShapeUtil` and HLO pass preservation and guards, `CommonPjRtClient::CopyToMemorySpace`, `_hlo.pyi` stubgen, and Python `xc.Layout` round-trips in unit tests.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
new `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

All of this lives in `GpuExecutable`, `Executable` only sees the module through
the virtual accessors. The build-once state (mutex, factory, sticky error and
the built module) is in a separate heap-allocated struct, so executables
without a serialized module don't pay for it. Readers like `shared_module()`
don't take the lock. Until the module is built, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the
serialized module (the config with the same debug options the built module
gets) and from the output info, so asking for them doesn't build the module.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012082361

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Derive GpuExecutable from Executable directly

head_commit.message:
Derive GpuExecutable from Executable directly

`GpuExecutable` now derives from the abstract `Executable` instead of
`HloModuleExecutable`. It keeps its optional `HloModule` and its `ModuleStats`
itself and implements `shared_module()`, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()`, `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()`.

If the executable has the module, these return the module's values, exactly as
before. Without the module (`embed_hlo_module=false`, or a `GpuExecutableProto`
without a serialized module), the executable answers from what it keeps:

- The input/output aliasing is rebuilt from the output info, which is already
  part of `GpuExecutableProto`.
- `module_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the new
  `GpuExecutable::Params::module_config` and `Params::buffer_donor_config`,
  which `GpuCompiler` fills from the module when it doesn't embed it.
  `module_config()` still CHECK-fails if neither is there, as today.

This way callers can get the metadata of an executable compiled with
`embed_hlo_module=false` through the `Executable` interface, and
`GpuExecutable` no longer needs `HloModuleExecutable`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

MoveUserInstructionsIn previously tried to predict whether tuple_use would become dead using only tuple_use->user_count() == 1, eagerly dropping its tuple slot and shifting later GTE indices before dead instructions were removed. That silently miscompiled when a sibling GTE read the same tuple_index, corrupted a live ROOT GTE before RunImpl crashed trying to remove it via user_count() == 0, and missed compacting multi-user GTEs whose consumers all moved in.

Always append moved-in results in MoveUserInstructionsIn while preserving existing slots, shardings, and OriginalValue entries in place, guard RunImpl removals with IsDead() and IsSafelyRemovable(), and compact unused branch outputs once in RemoveUnusedBranchOutputs from the actual surviving GTE users (updating tuple shardings and remapping kept OriginalValue subtrees via CopyOriginalValue).

display_title: [IFRT] Validate `ConcreteSharding` and `ConcreteShardingSpec` shard counts and index domains

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate `ConcreteSharding` and `ConcreteShardingSpec` shard counts and index domains

`ConcreteSharding` deferred checking shard-shape and index-domain counts to `Disassemble` and `IndexDomains`, and neither `ConcreteSharding` nor `ConcreteShardingSpec` verified that provided `index_domains` matched `shard_shapes`, matched the requested `shape` (including in `GetShardShape`), or lay within the logical `shape`.

Validate at `ConcreteShardingSpec::CreateIfValid`, `ConcreteSharding::CreateIfValid`, and `ConcreteSharding::WithDeviceAssignment` that shard-shape counts match either all devices or addressable devices (short-circuiting before `AddressableDeviceList()` when matching all devices, and avoiding a duplicate `AddressableDeviceList()` lookup on error in `ConcreteShardingSpec::ToSharding`), and validate eagerly when `index_domains` is present that its size matches `shard_shapes`, each entry's shape matches the corresponding shard shape, and every entry is contained within `shape`. Reject mismatched `shape` arguments in `IndexDomains` and `GetShardShape`, support both all-shards and addressable-only `ConcreteSharding` representations consistently in `Disassemble` and `IndexDomains`, and update unit test fixtures in `array_impl_test_lib.cc` (which previously passed mixed shard-shape and index-domain counts) and tests whose `index_domains` extended past `Shape({30})`.

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data

caller in XLA reads it anymore. `buffer_assignment_proto()` returns the same as

display_title: [XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Compact unused conditional outputs after MoveUserInstructionsIn.

MoveUserInstructionsIn previously tried to predict whether tuple_use would become dead using only tuple_use->user_count() == 1, eagerly dropping its tuple slot and shifting later GTE indices before dead instructions were removed. That silently miscompiled when a sibling GTE read the same tuple_index, corrupted a live ROOT GTE before RunImpl crashed trying to remove it via user_count() == 0, and missed compacting multi-user GTEs whose consumers all moved in.

Always append moved-in results in MoveUserInstructionsIn while preserving existing slots, shardings, and OriginalValue entries in place, guard RunImpl removals with IsDead() and IsSafelyRemovable(), and compact unused branch outputs once in RemoveUnusedBranchOutputs from the actual surviving GTE users (updating tuple shardings and remapping kept OriginalValue subtrees via CopyOriginalValue).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.
- Disables SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes cl/959445928, i.e.
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

head_commit.message:
Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The HLO that goes into HLO snapshots is debug state of whoever runs
the executable, so it moves out of `Executable::hlo_proto_`:

- `Service::BuildExecutable` returns the HLO before optimizations (plus the
  buffer assignment after optimizations) through an optional out-param instead
  of `set_hlo_proto`. `Service::Compile` keeps it in the `CompilationCache`
  entry, and `Service::Execute` reads it from there.
- `LocalExecutable` gets an optional snapshot HLO, filled through a new
  optional out-param of `LocalService::CompileExecutables`. Executables loaded
  with `LocalClient::Load` don't have one.
- New free helpers in `xla/service/executable.h`: `DumpingHloSnapshots()`
  replaces `Executable::dumping_snapshot()` at these call sites, and
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()` builds the snapshot HLO from the executable's
  HloModule and buffer assignment if nobody kept one.
- The HLO before optimizations is only built if `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots` is
  set, since snapshots are its only reader.
- The CPU AOT loader no longer attaches a full HloProto when dumping snapshots;
  the fallback above produces the same content.
- Deletes the unused `HloRunnerLegacy::HloProtoFromWrapped`.

Behaviour change: snapshot paths that dereferenced a null `hlo_proto()` before
(e.g. CPU without `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, GPU executables loaded from a
proto, `Service::ExecuteGraphParallel` on CPU) now dump the optimized HloModule
instead of crashing. On CPU with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, these snapshots
now keep literal payloads. Snapshots that contain the HLO before optimizations
today still do. Since `Service` no longer replaces the executable's HloProto,
TF's `get_compiler_ir` with `OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED` now returns the
optimized module also when dumping is enabled. It returned the module before
optimizations in that case, which was a bug.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

`IndexDomain` permitted `origin` and `shape` with mismatched numbers of dimensions and allowed `origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]` to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (and their cumulative non-zero product to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` or overflow `int64_t`), forcing `Intersect` and `Contains` to repeat per-operand checks on the number of dimensions while allowing domains that cannot fit inside any valid `Shape`.

Add `IndexDomain::Create` to validate `origin.elements().size() == shape.dims().size()` and that the cumulative product of non-zero upper-bound dimensions (`origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]`) does not exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements`, validate `IndexDomain(origin, shape)` and `operator+=` with `CHECK_OK` via a shared helper, route `IndexDomain::FromProto` through `IndexDomain::Create`, construct non-empty `Intersect` results via `UncheckedTag`, and drop redundant per-operand dimension-count checks in `Intersect` and `Contains`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

head_commit.message:
Make Executable::buffer_assignment_proto() virtual

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. `hlo_proto_` on the base mixes up two things: the buffer assignment
that the backend owns, and an HLO snapshot that the creator attaches for
dumping. This CL starts to pull them apart.

`Executable::buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes virtual. The default still
reads `hlo_proto_`. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` override it from state
they own, and return it in exactly the cases where the base accessor returns
non-null today:

- `GpuExecutable` returns its buffer assignment proto only if the compiler
  embeds debug info and keeps the HloModule
  (`Params::expose_buffer_assignment_proto`). Executables loaded from a proto
  still return nullptr. The always-available GPU accessor is renamed to
  `owned_buffer_assignment_proto()`, because a non-virtual accessor with the
  same name would hide the virtual one.
- `CpuExecutable` gets an optional buffer assignment proto that the CPU
  compiler sets with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, and the CPU AOT loader with
  `xla_embed_ir_in_executable` or `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots`.

The compilers still call `set_hlo_proto`; that goes away in a follow-up.

No behaviour change.

display_title: Add `is_mutable` parameter to `PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`.

head_commit.message:
Add `is_mutable` parameter to `PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`.

`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` previously hardcoded
`is_mutable=false` when calling `ImportForeignMemory`. GPU ignored the flag,
while `CpuRawBuffer` honored it, so donating a view on PjRt CPU always
allocated a new output buffer instead of aliasing caller memory in place.
Unconditionally flipping `is_mutable` to `true` could surprise callers that
rely on read-only CPU views (such as NumPy or DLPack interop).

Thread an explicit `bool is_mutable` parameter through
`PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` (keeping the existing overload
defaulting to `is_mutable=false` for backwards compatibility),
`CommonPjRtClient`, `TfPjRtClient`, `PjRtCApiClient`, and the PJRT C API
v0.119 (`PJRT_Client_CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer_Args::is_mutable`). Callers
that want in-place donation on CPU can opt in with `is_mutable=true`, while
existing callers keep read-only CPU views by default.

Also avoid wrapping an empty `std::function<void()>` (`nullptr`) into a
non-empty `absl::AnyInvocable<void() &&>` in
`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`, which previously threw
`std::bad_function_call` on buffer destruction when `on_delete_callback` was
null.

display_title: Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

head_commit.message:
Move the HloModule logic of Executable into HloModuleExecutable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. With the HloModule stored in the base class, every executable
had to carry one to answer metadata queries.

Move `hlo_module_` and `module_stats_` and the implementations that read them
into `HloModuleExecutable`:

- `shared_module()` (nullable), `module_config()`, `result_shape()`,
  `compute_computation_layout()`, `name()`, `input_output_alias_config()`,
  `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()` are pure virtual on
  `Executable`. `set_module_stats()` lives on `HloModuleExecutable`.
- `module()` and `has_module()` stay as non-virtual helpers on top of a new
  protected pure virtual `module_ptr()`, so they don't copy a
  `std::shared_ptr`.
- Virtuals that don't need state keep their defaults
  (`SizeOfGeneratedCodeInBytes()`, `GetAllocations()`, ...).
- The unused `execution_count_` is deleted.

The only state left in `Executable` is the HLO proto for debugging
(`hlo_proto_` and its mutex). It still fills in the module lazily through
`module()`. Later changes move its producers and readers away and remove it.

`HloModuleExecutable` implements everything from the module as before, so
there is no behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that
derive from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable`
instead (or implement the new pure virtuals).

display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` previously hardcoded
`is_mutable=false` when calling `ImportForeignMemory`. GPU ignored the flag,
while `CpuRawBuffer` honored it, so donating a view on PjRt CPU always
allocated a new output buffer instead of aliasing caller memory in place.
Unconditionally flipping `is_mutable` to `true` could surprise callers that
rely on read-only CPU views (such as NumPy or DLPack interop).

Thread an explicit `bool is_mutable` parameter through
`PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` (keeping the existing overload
defaulting to `is_mutable=false` for backwards compatibility),
`CommonPjRtClient`, `TfPjRtClient`, `PjRtCApiClient`, and the PJRT C API
v0.119 (`PJRT_Client_CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer_Args::is_mutable`). Callers
that want in-place donation on CPU can opt in with `is_mutable=true`, while
existing callers keep read-only CPU views by default.

Also avoid wrapping an empty `std::function<void()>` (`nullptr`) into a
non-empty `absl::AnyInvocable<void() &&>` in
`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`, which previously threw
`std::bad_function_call` on buffer destruction when `on_delete_callback` was
null.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Emit aligned atomic loads and monotonic CPU atomics in lower_tensors

Replace the plain `llvm.load` seed loads in `RewriteAtomicStore`,
`RewriteAtomicRMW::rewriteAsAtomicCAS`, and `RewriteSetDynamicDimSize`, plus
the pre check `f32` load in `RewriteAtomicRMW::rewriteAtomicFMaxAsIntAtomics`,
with naturally aligned atomic loads, and reuse `GetAtomicSyncScope` in
`RewriteSetDynamicDimSize`. Emit `unordered` ordering on CUDA and Intel GPU,
`syncscope("agent-one-as") monotonic` on AMDGPU, and `monotonic` across CPU
atomic loads and direct stores so LLVM `LoopIdiomRecognizePass` cannot form
unresolved `__llvm_memcpy_element_unordered_atomic_*` calls in the XLA:CPU JIT.

display_title: Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

head_commit.message:
Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

A deserialized GpuExecutable still needs the HLO module to compute the module fingerprint and to decide whether collectives should use minimal GPU resources. Both are pure functions of the optimized module, so we can compute them at compile time and store them in `GpuExecutableProto` (xla/service/gpu/gpu_executable.proto) instead.

This change adds the `fingerprint` and `collective_use_minimal_resource` fields, writes them in `ToProto` and uses them in `FromProto`. `GpuExecutable::Create` computes the fingerprint from the module unless it's passed in, which happens when deserializing and when the compiler doesn't embed the module. Executables serialized before these fields existed fall back to computing the values from the HLO module, which is still deserialized eagerly for now. Executables without an HLO module have an empty fingerprint and always write `collective_use_minimal_resource=false`, which is the value they used before. If `Params::hlo_module` only holds the serialized module (nothing does that yet), `Create` requires `collective_use_minimal_resource` to be set, because we don't want to build the module just for that and silently using false could differ from what the module would give.

Computing the fingerprint eagerly costs 0.1-0.45% of the JIT compile time (measured on H100 for gemma4_2b, maxtext and a chain of 500 dots, with and without autotuning). That's cheap enough to not justify a lazily computed and cached value.

The fingerprint stored at compile time matches the fingerprint of the module after a serialization round trip (which is what PjRt computed for deserialized executables so far). A new PjRt test checks that for a few non-trivial programs, and I also verified it for all GPU AOT goldens.

The AOT golden comparison ignores both fields since they are derived from the HLO module, which is already ignored.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

Enforcing element-type and per-shard-shape equality on `io_aliases` at IR verification missed impossible cross-device and host-to-device aliases while rejecting valid bitcast-style and layout-changing aliases.

`IfrtCallOpInterface` verification now drops the element-type and per-shard-shape equality checks and instead requires XLA array element types (rejecting `!ifrt.token` and `!ifrt.string`), matching devices, and matching effective memory kinds.

Physical per-shard byte-size compatibility depends on target-specific layout tiling and sub-byte packing, so it is deferred to atom-program compilation (e.g., XLA after layout assignment) or the underlying IFRT runtime for externally bound executables, matching `ifrt.BitcastArrays`.

Also updates `ProgramInterpreter` and `ProgramMemoryTracer` to use the `IfrtCallOpInterface` alias helpers (`GetDonatedOrAliasedInputIndices` and `getIoAliasPairs`), and adds `ProgramMemoryTracer` test coverage for aliased offloaded arrays and aliased arrays with differing dtypes, shapes, and layouts.

head_commit.message:
Move ORC loading out of `CpuAotLoader` behind `FunctionLibraryLoader` AOT runtimes shouldn't pull in ORC (and most of LLVM) just to load precompiled kernels. So now: 1. `CpuAotLoader` takes a `FunctionLibraryLoader` callback to construct the `FunctionLibrary` from the proto. 2. The existing (ORC-based) loader is moved to a standalone target. 3. `CpuCompiler` and `XlaAotFunction` pass the loader down the stack to `CpuAotLoader`. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["XlaAotFunction / HostOffloading"]:::caller C["CpuCompiler"]:::caller subgraph core ["ORC-free"] N["NanoRtExecutable"]:::orcfree L["CpuAotLoader"]:::orcfree F["(new) FunctionLibraryLoader"]:::contract end O["(new) orc_function_library_loader
(LLVM ORC)"]:::orc A --> N N --> L C --> L L --> F A -->|"depends on ORC"| O C -->|"depends on ORC"| O classDef caller fill:#F3E8FD,stroke:#8430CE,color:#3C1053,stroke-width:1.5px classDef orcfree fill:#CEEAD6,stroke:#137333,color:#0D652D,stroke-width:2px classDef contract fill:#D2E3FC,stroke:#1A73E8,color:#174EA6,stroke-width:2px classDef orc fill:#FAD2CF,stroke:#C5221F,color:#A50E0E,stroke-width:2px ``` Also the hlo_module in `CpuAotLoader::LoadAotCompilationResults` was never actually used, so removed it. display_title: [IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Verify devices, memory kind, and per-shard byte size for `io_aliases`

Aliasing an input to an output on `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` requires the two buffers to reside on the same devices and memory kind, while allowing different element types, per-shard shapes, and layouts as long as their per-shard byte size matches. Enforcing only element-type and per-shard-shape equality missed impossible cross-device and host-to-device aliases while rejecting valid bitcast-style or layout-changing aliases.

`IfrtCallOpInterface` verification now requires XLA array element types (rejecting `!ifrt.token` and `!ifrt.string`), matching devices, and matching effective memory kinds, and drops the element-type and per-shard-shape equality requirements.

Per-shard byte-size equality is checked statically when both shardings are specified and both layouts are either `default` or unmodified untiled user-specified layouts (without `:L(...)`, `:E(...)`, `:SC(...)`, or `:M(...)` modifiers). All other pairs—tiled, modified-untiled, `auto`, mixed (`default`/user-specified), or unspecified-sharding—defer byte-size verification to atom-program compilation (e.g., XLA after layout assignment) or the underlying IFRT runtime for externally bound executables.

display_title: Derive GpuExecutable from Executable directly

head_commit.message:
Derive GpuExecutable from Executable directly

`GpuExecutable` now derives from the abstract `Executable` instead of
`HloModuleExecutable`. It keeps its optional `HloModule` and its `ModuleStats`
itself and implements `shared_module()`, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()`, `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()`.

If the executable has the module, these return the module's values, exactly as
before. Without the module (`embed_hlo_module=false`, or a `GpuExecutableProto`
without a serialized module), the executable answers from what it keeps:

- The input/output aliasing is rebuilt from the output info, which is already
  part of `GpuExecutableProto`.
- `module_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the new
  `GpuExecutable::Params::module_config` and `Params::buffer_donor_config`,
  which `GpuCompiler` fills from the module when it doesn't embed it.
  `module_config()` still CHECK-fails if neither is there, as today.

This way callers can get the metadata of an executable compiled with
`embed_hlo_module=false` through the `Executable` interface, and
`GpuExecutable` no longer needs `HloModuleExecutable`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
new `GpuExecutable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

All of this lives in `GpuExecutable`, `Executable` only sees the module through
the virtual accessors. The build-once state (mutex, factory, sticky error and
the built module) is in a separate heap-allocated struct, so executables
without a serialized module don't pay for it. Readers like `shared_module()`
don't take the lock. Until the module is built, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the
serialized module (the config with the same debug options the built module
gets) and from the output info, so asking for them doesn't build the module.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Emit aligned atomic loads and monotonic CPU atomics in lower_tensors

Replace the plain `llvm.load` seed loads in `RewriteAtomicStore`,
`RewriteAtomicRMW::rewriteAsAtomicCAS`, and `RewriteSetDynamicDimSize`, plus
the pre check `f32` load in `RewriteAtomicRMW::rewriteAtomicFMaxAsIntAtomics`,
with naturally aligned atomic loads, and reuse `GetAtomicSyncScope` in
`RewriteSetDynamicDimSize`. Emit `unordered` ordering on CUDA and Intel GPU,
`syncscope("agent-one-as") monotonic` on AMDGPU, and `monotonic` across CPU
atomic loads and direct stores so LLVM `LoopIdiomRecognizePass` cannot form
unresolved `__llvm_memcpy_element_unordered_atomic_*` calls in the XLA:CPU JIT.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten `IfrtArrayType` element-type and layout verification

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten `IfrtArrayType` element-type and layout verification

`IfrtArrayType::verify` accepted any `mlir::BuiltinDialect` element type (allowing non-XLA types like `vector`, `i128`, `f128`, and `complex<i32>`) and relied solely on `xla::LayoutMode::FromString`'s syntactic parsing for user-specified layouts. As a result, unsupported element types, non-default layouts on token/string arrays, and malformed XLA layouts (mismatched rank, out-of-bounds/duplicate dimensions, invalid tiles, negative `element_size_in_bits`, or out-of-bounds `split_configs`) passed verification and could fail or corrupt shape-size calculations in downstream passes.

`IfrtArrayType::verify` now requires non-token, non-string element types to satisfy `xla::primitive_util::IsArrayType(xla::ConvertMlirTypeToPrimitiveType(element_type))` and rejects any non-default layout mode on `!ifrt.token` and `!ifrt.string` arrays. For user-specified layouts on XLA array types, it checks sharding compatibility before layout validation, enforces exact rank (`minor_to_major().size() == shape.getRank()`) so layouts with empty `minor_to_major` (such as `"{:S(1)}"`) are rejected on non-scalar shapes, and validates the layout via `xla::LayoutUtil::ValidateLayoutForShape` against the per-shard `xla::Shape` when divisible (falling back to the global shape for non-divisible shardings and `#ifrt.sharding_unspecified`).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Memoize subcomputation properties in HloCostAnalysis

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Memoize subcomputation properties in HloCostAnalysis

`HloRematerialization` runs `HloCostAnalysis` across every computation in module post order. `HloCostAnalysis::ProcessSubcomputation` previously allocated a nested visitor, rewalked each callee, and copied `hlo_properties_` into the caller on every control flow or fusion edge, causing superquadratic or exponential compile time on nested `while` and `conditional` graphs and shared callees.

Cache completed computation totals in `subcomputation_properties_` during `FinishVisit`, evaluate uncached module subcomputations in place while saving traversal state on the stack, and invalidate cached totals in `RemoveInstruction` and across module switches. Generated HLO and cost values are unchanged.

Tests:
* `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service:hlo_cost_analysis_test`: pins single visit post order and shared DAG traversal, nested `RevisitInstruction` cache invalidation, partial subgraph visits, and cross module reuse.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Remove Executable::hlo_proto_ and make Executable an abstract base class

head_commit.message:
Remove Executable::hlo_proto_ and make Executable an abstract base class

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. `hlo_proto_` (with its mutex) is the last data member of
`Executable`, and all its producers and readers have moved away:

- Backends override the virtual `buffer_assignment_proto()` with state they
  own.
- HLO snapshots use the HLO that `Service` or `LocalExecutable` keep, or
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()`.
- `DumpingHloSnapshots()` replaces `dumping_snapshot()`.

So remove `set_hlo_proto()`, `hlo_proto()`, `dumping_snapshot()`, `hlo_proto_`
and its mutex. With that, `Executable` is an abstract base class without data
members, and `buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes pure virtual.
`HloModuleExecutable` returns nullptr, the backends that keep a buffer
assignment override it.

No behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that derive
from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable` instead
(or implement the pure virtuals).

display_title: [NFC] Move `HloValue` state from `BufferAllocation` to `BufferAssignment`

head_commit.message:
[NFC] Move `HloValue` state from `BufferAllocation` to `BufferAssignment`

`BufferAllocation` is used by runtime targets that only need allocation metadata and slices, so it shouldn't depend on `HloValue` (which pulls in `hlo/ir:hlo`).

We move the per-allocation `HloValue` state and heap traces into a parallel `allocation_values_` vector in `BufferAssignment` (indexed by `BufferAllocation::index()`) and remove the `HloValue` accessors from `BufferAllocation`.

We keep serializing `assigned` inside `BufferAllocationProto` (populated by `BufferAssignment::ToProto()`, while standalone `BufferAllocation::ToProto()` leaves it empty) rather than moving it onto `BufferAssignmentProto` for now. Several `HloProto` consumers (e.g. XProf and `ComputePeakMemorySizes`) read `BufferAllocationProto.assigned` directly instead of going through `BufferAssignment::FromProto()`. Switching the writer right away would also break CPU/GPU AOT forward compatibility when older readers load new protos, so moving the proto field would require a multi-stage rollout across repos.

A follow up CL will actually split the files

display_title: [TFLite YNNPACK] Lower MoE experts with ragged_dot and blockwise quantization.

head_commit.message:
[TFLite YNNPACK] Lower MoE experts with ragged_dot and blockwise quantization.
Previously, `DefineMoeNode` split MoE execution between host-side padded token bucketing (`[E, C, D]`) for multi-token prefill when `expert_indices` was a partition input and a weight-gather fallback for single-token decode or partition-internal `expert_indices`, which copied selected expert weights per token and prevented static `pack_b` and column-sum constant folding on blockwise-quantized weights.
- Unify `DefineMoeNode` in the TFLite YNNPACK delegate to lower `odml.moe_experts` ops (decode and prefill, symmetric `AffineQuantization`, `MultiAxisQuantization`, and `BlockwiseQuantization` in `int8` and `int4`) via `ynn_define_ragged_dot` and `ynn::define_blockwise_dot` over host-partitioned `[B * N * K, D]` expert slots and stationary 3D `[E, D_in, D_out]` weights.
- Trace partition-internal `RESHAPE` and `EXPAND_DIMS` views on `expert_indices` back to the external partition input (or constant) tensor, while rejecting MoE nodes whose `expert_indices` is produced by non-view partition ops.
- Flatten the MoE combine reduction from 4D `[B, N, K, D_out]` to 3D `[B * N, K, D_out]` followed by `ynn_define_split_dim` back to `[B, N, D_out]`, avoiding an outer loop over `B` and skipping YNNPACK subgraph rebuilds in `Prepare` when only sequence length `N` changes.
- Replace padded host token bucketing in `MoeDispatch`, `SetupMoeDispatch`, and `SetMoeDispatchShapes` with flat slot partitioning, removing `ShouldDispatchMoeOnHost`, `SetMoeDispatchData`, and `dispatch_moe_on_host`.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten `IfrtArrayType` element-type and layout verification

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten `IfrtArrayType` element-type and layout verification

`IfrtArrayType::verify` accepted any `mlir::BuiltinDialect` element type (allowing non-XLA types like `vector`, `i128`, `f128`, and `complex<i32>`) and relied solely on `xla::LayoutMode::FromString`'s syntactic parsing for user-specified layouts. As a result, unsupported element types, non-default layouts on token/string arrays, and malformed XLA layouts (mismatched rank, out-of-bounds/duplicate dimensions, invalid tiles, negative `element_size_in_bits`, or out-of-bounds `split_configs`) passed verification and could fail or corrupt shape-size calculations in downstream passes.

`IfrtArrayType::verify` now requires non-token, non-string element types to satisfy `xla::primitive_util::IsArrayType(xla::ConvertMlirTypeToPrimitiveType(element_type))` and rejects any non-default layout mode on `!ifrt.token` and `!ifrt.string` arrays. For user-specified layouts on XLA array types, it checks sharding compatibility before layout validation, enforces exact rank (`minor_to_major().size() == shape.getRank()`) so layouts with empty `minor_to_major` (such as `"{:S(1)}"`) are rejected on non-scalar shapes, and validates the layout via `xla::LayoutUtil::ValidateLayoutForShape` against the per-shard `xla::Shape` when divisible (falling back to the global shape for non-divisible shardings and `#ifrt.sharding_unspecified`).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Sink large broadcast fills from scalar cones and small parameters.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Sink large broadcast fills from scalar cones and small parameters.

Previously, `IsLargeIndependentFill` (`HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands`)
required every operand of a large (≥ 1 MiB) `kLoop` fusion to be a direct
scalar constant or effective parameter. Consequently, the GPU latency-hiding
scheduler did not mark broadcast fills `ForceEarly(true)` when their scalar
operand was produced by pure scalar arithmetic (such as negating or scaling a
runtime scalar argument) or when they broadcast a small non-scalar parameter
(such as a 2 KiB parameter vector into a 1 MiB matrix). Because these fusions
have `AsyncDepth == 0`, bottom-up scheduling deferred them behind `while` loops
and collective regions, floating their multi-megabyte output buffers to the top
of the computation.

Replace `HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands` with
`HasOnlyIndependentAmplifiedOperands` and `IsIndependentScalarSubgraph` in
`IsLargeIndependentFill` so the scheduler also sinks large (≥ 1 MiB) loop
fusions whose inputs are amplified by at least 100x
(`kMinFillAmplificationFactor = 100`) and consist solely of constants,
effective parameters, or bounded synchronous scalar ancestor cones
(`kMaxScalarConeNodes = 16` elementwise, bitcast, or reshape instructions).
Requiring every node in a computed operand's ancestor cone to be a synchronous
effective scalar guarantees zero collective async depth (`AsyncDepth == 0`)
before `InitializeGraphAnalysis` runs and prevents sinking fusions whose scalar
operand derives from reducing or slicing a large upstream tensor, which would
extend the upstream tensor's live range. On a 1 MiB (`f32[512,512]`) broadcast
fill fed by a negated scalar parameter across a `while` loop, sinking the fill
right before its consumer reduces scheduled peak live memory by 33.3% (from
3.00 MiB to 2.00 MiB).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1028401365

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Stop calling Executable::set_hlo_proto in the GPU and CPU compilers

head_commit.message:
Stop calling Executable::set_hlo_proto in the GPU and CPU compilers

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The GPU and CPU compilers only attached an `HloProto` so that the
base class could answer `buffer_assignment_proto()` and so that HLO snapshots
had something to read. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` now override
`buffer_assignment_proto()` themselves, and snapshots no longer read
`Executable::hlo_proto()`, so the compilers stop calling `set_hlo_proto`.

`Executable::hlo_proto()` now returns nullptr for GPU and CPU executables. No
caller in XLA reads it anymore. `buffer_assignment_proto()` returns the same as
before.

display_title: [XLA:PjRt] Tighten transpose kernel target gating and helpers

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PjRt] Tighten transpose kernel target gating and helpers

Follow up cleanups to the 512 bit transpose microkernels:

* Match `HWY_AVX3_SPR` with `==` instead of `<=` and guard x86 cache and strip heuristics with `HWY_ARCH_X86`. `HWY_AVX10_2` and future 64 byte non x86 targets now default to the 512 bit kernels instead of inheriting SPR workarounds.
* Split microkernel selection into one function per row width (`TransposeRows64`, `TransposeRows32`, `TransposeRows16`) behind a flat `TransposeMicroKernel` dispatcher, with the L1D conflict test in `HasX86L1dConflict512`. This does not change the generated x86 code.
* Rewrite the generic `ConcatEvenOddBlocks` fallback recursively over `hn::Half<D>` instead of `hn::ExtractBlock`. This avoids an RVV `LMUL` mismatch in `hn::Combine` and rejects scalable tags.
* Call `f` directly inside the `ForEachIndexedImpl` fold expression to avoid forwarding `f` across multiple pack elements.

Existing x86 behavior up to `HWY_AVX3_SPR` is unchanged.

Tests:
* `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/pjrt:transpose_kernels_test` verifies all microkernel and macrokernel shapes and stride branches across generated Highway targets.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

Whether a computation is embedded cannot be determined from its direct callers
alone: a `while`, `conditional`, or `call` body inside a `map`, `sort`, or
`reduce` has a `CallContext::kControlFlow` direct caller even though it executes
inside an embedded computation. `CallGraph` already computes transitive
`CallContext` in one pass over the module.

- Add `CallGraphNode::IsEmbedded()` to check whether a computation is in an
  embedded context (`CallContext::kEmbedded` or `CallContext::kBoth`).
- Use `CallGraphNode::IsEmbedded()` in `InstructionFusion`, `MultiOutputFusion`,
  and `EmbeddedWhileLoopUnroller` instead of
  `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.
- Add `ScatterExpander::kEliminateEmbeddedScatters` backed by `CallGraph` and
  use it in `CpuCompiler` so transitively embedded scatters are expanded too.
- Remove `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.

Note on behavior change: this is not purely a refactor for non-CPU backends.
Control-flow bodies nested inside embedded computations (e.g. a `while`,
`conditional`, or `call` inside a `reduce`/`sort`/`map` body) were previously
fused by `InstructionFusion` and `MultiOutputFusion` on GPU/TPU and now will not
be.

display_title: [XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

Whether a computation is embedded cannot be determined from its direct callers
alone: a `while`, `conditional`, or `call` body inside a `map`, `sort`, or
`reduce` has a `CallContext::kControlFlow` direct caller even though it executes
inside an embedded computation. `CallGraph` already computes transitive
`CallContext` in one pass over the module.

- Add `CallGraphNode::IsEmbedded()` to check whether a computation is in an
  embedded context (`CallContext::kEmbedded` or `CallContext::kBoth`).
- Use `CallGraphNode::IsEmbedded()` in `InstructionFusion`, `MultiOutputFusion`,
  and `EmbeddedWhileLoopUnroller` instead of
  `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.
- Add `ScatterExpander::kEliminateEmbeddedScatters` backed by `CallGraph` and
  use it in `CpuCompiler` so transitively embedded scatters are expanded too.
- Remove `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.

Note on behavior change: this is not purely a refactor for non-CPU backends.
Control-flow bodies nested inside embedded computations (e.g. a `while`,
`conditional`, or `call` inside a `reduce`/`sort`/`map` body) were previously
fused by `InstructionFusion` and `MultiOutputFusion` on GPU/TPU and now will not
be.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PjRt] Tighten transpose kernel target gating and helpers

Follow up cleanups to the 512 bit transpose microkernels:

* Match `HWY_AVX3_SPR` with `==` instead of `<=` and guard x86 cache and strip heuristics with `HWY_ARCH_X86`. `HWY_AVX10_2` and future 64 byte non x86 targets now default to the 512 bit kernels instead of inheriting SPR workarounds.
* Split microkernel selection into one function per row width (`TransposeRows64`, `TransposeRows32`, `TransposeRows16`) behind a flat `TransposeMicroKernel` dispatcher, with the L1D conflict test in `HasX86L1dConflict512`. This does not change the generated x86 code.
* Rewrite the generic `ConcatEvenOddBlocks` fallback recursively over `hn::Half<D>` instead of `hn::ExtractBlock`. This avoids an RVV `LMUL` mismatch in `hn::Combine` and rejects scalable tags.
* Call `f` directly inside the `ForEachIndexedImpl` fold expression to avoid forwarding `f` across multiple pack elements.

Existing x86 behavior up to `HWY_AVX3_SPR` is unchanged.

Tests:
* `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/pjrt:transpose_kernels_test` verifies all microkernel and macrokernel shapes and stride branches across generated Highway targets.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Generalize IsLargeIndependentFill to sink scalar-parameter fills.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Generalize IsLargeIndependentFill to sink scalar-parameter fills.

Previously, `IsLargeIndependentFill` in
`xla/service/gpu/gpu_latency_hiding_scheduler.cc` required
`instr.operand_count() == 0`, which excluded large (≥ 1 MiB) loop fusions that
broadcast dynamic scalar parameters (such as runtime mask values, step scales,
or tuple-unpacked scalar arguments). Because those fusions have
`AsyncDepth == 0`, the bottom-up latency-hiding scheduler deferred them behind
`while` loops and collective regions, floating their multi-megabyte output
buffers to the top of the computation.

Generalize `IsLargeIndependentFill` via `HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands` to
accept loop fusions whose operands are all effective scalars that are constants
or effective parameters (`hlo_query::IsEffectiveParameter`). Because constant
and effective-parameter scalar operands have zero upstream compute or
collective dependencies and negligible live buffer footprints, marking these
fills `ForceEarly(true)` sinks them next to their consumers without delaying
async collective starts. On a 512x512 `f32` (1 MiB) broadcast fill consumed
after a `while` loop, this reduces peak live memory pressure from 3 MiB to
2 MiB (-33%) while preserving the full 1,002-cycle `while` and `all-reduce`
overlap.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Sink large broadcast fills from scalar cones and small parameters.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Sink large broadcast fills from scalar cones and small parameters.

Previously, `IsLargeIndependentFill` (`HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands`)
required every operand of a large (≥ 1 MiB) `kLoop` fusion to be a direct
scalar constant or effective parameter. Consequently, the GPU latency-hiding
scheduler did not mark broadcast fills `ForceEarly(true)` when their scalar
operand was produced by pure scalar arithmetic (such as negating or scaling a
runtime scalar argument) or when they broadcast a small non-scalar parameter
(such as a 2 KiB parameter vector into a 1 MiB matrix). Because these fusions
have `AsyncDepth == 0`, bottom-up scheduling deferred them behind `while` loops
and collective regions, floating their multi-megabyte output buffers to the top
of the computation.

Replace `HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands` with
`HasOnlyIndependentAmplifiedOperands` and `IsIndependentScalarSubgraph` in
`IsLargeIndependentFill` so the scheduler also sinks large (≥ 1 MiB) loop
fusions whose inputs are amplified by at least 100x
(`kMinFillAmplificationFactor = 100`) and consist solely of constants,
effective parameters, or bounded synchronous scalar ancestor cones
(`kMaxScalarConeNodes = 16` elementwise, bitcast, or reshape instructions).
Requiring every node in a computed operand's ancestor cone to be a synchronous
effective scalar guarantees zero collective async depth (`AsyncDepth == 0`)
before `InitializeGraphAnalysis` runs and prevents sinking fusions whose scalar
operand derives from reducing or slicing a large upstream tensor, which would
extend the upstream tensor's live range. On a 1 MiB (`f32[512,512]`) broadcast
fill fed by a negated scalar parameter across a `while` loop, sinking the fill
right before its consumer reduces scheduled peak live memory by 33.3% (from
3.00 MiB to 2.00 MiB).

display_title: Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

head_commit.message:
Let Service and LocalExecutable own the HLO snapshot instead of Executable

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The HLO that goes into HLO snapshots is debug state of whoever runs
the executable, so it moves out of `Executable::hlo_proto_`:

- `Service::BuildExecutable` returns the HLO before optimizations (plus the
  buffer assignment after optimizations) through an optional out-param instead
  of `set_hlo_proto`. `Service::Compile` keeps it in the `CompilationCache`
  entry, and `Service::Execute` reads it from there.
- `LocalExecutable` gets an optional snapshot HLO, filled through a new
  optional out-param of `LocalService::CompileExecutables`. Executables loaded
  with `LocalClient::Load` don't have one.
- New free helpers in `xla/service/executable.h`: `DumpingHloSnapshots()`
  replaces `Executable::dumping_snapshot()` at these call sites, and
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()` builds the snapshot HLO from the executable's
  HloModule and buffer assignment if nobody kept one.
- The HLO before optimizations is only built if `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots` is
  set, since snapshots are its only reader.
- The CPU AOT loader no longer attaches a full HloProto when dumping snapshots;
  the fallback above produces the same content.
- Deletes the unused `HloRunnerLegacy::HloProtoFromWrapped`.

Behaviour change: snapshot paths that dereferenced a null `hlo_proto()` before
(e.g. CPU without `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, GPU executables loaded from a
proto, `Service::ExecuteGraphParallel` on CPU) now dump the optimized HloModule
instead of crashing. On CPU with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, these snapshots
now keep literal payloads. Snapshots that contain the HLO before optimizations
today still do. Since `Service` no longer replaces the executable's HloProto,
TF's `get_compiler_ir` with `OPTIMIZED_HLO_PROTO_SERIALIZED` now returns the
optimized module also when dumping is enabled. It returned the module before
optimizations in that case, which was a bug.

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build

members. `hlo_proto_` on the base mixes up two things: the buffer assignment
that the backend owns, and an HLO snapshot that the creator attaches for
dumping. This CL starts to pull them apart.

`Executable::buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes virtual. The default still
reads `hlo_proto_`. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` override it from state
they own, and return it in exactly the cases where the base accessor returns

  `owned_buffer_assignment_proto()`, because a non-virtual accessor with the
  same name would hide the virtual one.

  compiler sets with `xla_embed_ir_in_executable`, and the CPU AOT loader with
  `xla_embed_ir_in_executable` or `xla_dump_hlo_snapshots`.
