head_commit.message:
PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52875

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

Copybara import of the project:

--

head_commit.message:
PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52875

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

display_title: [XLA:SDY] Support JAX custom_partitioning in Shardy partitioner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SDY] Support JAX custom_partitioning in Shardy partitioner

When the Shardy partitioner is fully enabled, GSPMD is completely bypassed,
leaving `stablehlo.custom_call @CustomSPMDPartitioning` unpartitioned and
failing compilation. To support it, we change the following:

- **Partitioner-agnostic callback API**: Add
  `CustomCallPartitioner::SupportsMlirPartitioning()` and `PartitionToMlir()`
  (defaulting to `false` / `std::nullopt` for GSPMD-only C++ partitioners),
  share PJRT C-API callback marshaling in `CApiCustomCallPartitioner` between
  GSPMD and Shardy, and remove the now-unused HLO-based `PopulateArgs`
  overload.

- **Callback MLIR preparation & sharding import**: Extract shared tile
  factorization (`factorizeTileAssignmentToSdy`) into
  `stablehlo_round_trip/sharding_import_utils.{h,cc}`, handle matching-mesh V3
  `NamedSharding` directly with V2 fallback, upgrade VHLO, inline direct helper
  calls, and legalize CHLO and complex math in a single `PassManager`, remapping
  positive `channel_handle` IDs via `nextChannelId` and importing remaining
  private helpers (such as `stablehlo.composite` decompositions) into
  `symbolTable`.

- **Global-IR lowering (`resolvePermutationFactors`)**: Wire
  `custom_spmd_partitioning.{h,cc}` into `CustomCallPartitioningOpInterface`,
  rewriting custom-partitioned calls into operand `sdy.reshard` (when needed) +
  divisibility padding + `sdy.manual_computation` + slicing + result
  `sdy.reshard` (when needed).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Rematerialize copies of large iota fills in ConstantFillCopyRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Rematerialize copies of large iota fills in ConstantFillCopyRewriter.

When `CopyInsertion` duplicates a 0-operand `kIota` loop fusion (for example,
when an index tensor initializes a `while` loop carry and also feeds a consumer
outside the loop), `CopyFusion` folds the `kCopy` into the original fusion as a
multi-output tuple. That couples the two live ranges together at the earliest
consumer's timestamp and keeps the copied buffer live across the intervening
loop.

Extend `ConstantFillCopyRewriter` (`IsConstantOrIotaFillBody` in
`xla/backends/gpu/transforms/constant_fill_copy_rewriter.cc`) to recognize
0-operand `kIota` loop fusions (≥ 1 MiB) alongside scalar-constant broadcasts.
Replacing each `kCopy` with an independent 0-operand `kIota` fusion eliminates
the device-to-device HBM read at the copy site (cutting memory traffic for that
buffer by 50%, since `iota` synthesizes indices in registers) and allows the
scheduler to sink the rematerialized fill next to its consumer, reducing
scheduled peak live memory by the full buffer size (e.g., 1 MiB for an
`s32[512,512]` index grid).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Generalize IsLargeIndependentFill to sink scalar-parameter fills.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Generalize IsLargeIndependentFill to sink scalar-parameter fills.

Previously, `IsLargeIndependentFill` in
`xla/service/gpu/gpu_latency_hiding_scheduler.cc` required
`instr.operand_count() == 0`, which excluded large (≥ 1 MiB) loop fusions that
broadcast dynamic scalar parameters (such as runtime mask values, step scales,
or tuple-unpacked scalar arguments). Because those fusions have
`AsyncDepth == 0`, the bottom-up latency-hiding scheduler deferred them behind
`while` loops and collective regions, floating their multi-megabyte output
buffers to the top of the computation.

Generalize `IsLargeIndependentFill` via `HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands` to
accept loop fusions whose operands are all effective scalars that are constants
or effective parameters (`hlo_query::IsEffectiveParameter`). Because constant
and effective-parameter scalar operands have zero upstream compute or
collective dependencies and negligible live buffer footprints, marking these
fills `ForceEarly(true)` sinks them next to their consumers without delaying
async collective starts. On a 512x512 `f32` (1 MiB) broadcast fill consumed
after a `while` loop, this reduces peak live memory pressure from 3 MiB to
2 MiB (-33%) while preserving the full 1,002-cycle `while` and `all-reduce`
overlap.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten `IfrtArrayType` element-type and layout verification

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Verify element type and user-specified layout rank in `IfrtArrayType`

Accepting any `mlir::BuiltinDialect` element type in `IfrtArrayType::verify` allowed non-XLA types such as `index`, `vector`, `i128`, `f128`, and `complex<i32>` to parse into verified arrays, forcing downstream passes to guard element types ad hoc and leaving `ToIfrtDType` exposed to `PRIMITIVE_TYPE_INVALID`. Similarly, `xla::LayoutMode::FromString` validates syntax only, so user-specified layouts with a mismatched `minor_to_major` rank (such as a 2D layout on a 3D tensor) silently passed type verification.

`IfrtArrayType::verify` now requires non-token, non-string element types to satisfy `xla::primitive_util::IsArrayType(xla::ConvertMlirTypeToPrimitiveType(element_type))`, guaranteeing that every verified array maps to a valid non-`kInvalid` IFRT `DType`. For user-specified layouts, verification now rejects any layout whose `minor_to_major` size does not match the array rank.

Existing tests that relied on mismatched layout ranks (`ifrt_merge_ops.mlir`, `verify_call.mlir`, and `verify_call_loaded_executable.mlir`) are updated to use valid-rank or duplicate-dimension layouts, and `verify_array.mlir` adds positive and negative coverage for both checks.

head_commit.message:
PR #53038: Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively for non-ASCII paths

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53038

#ai-generated

**Status quo**
`WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory` and `WindowsFileSystem::DeleteRecursively` convert the wide-character path back to `std::string` by range-constructing it from the `std::wstring`, which keeps only the low byte of each wide character. Any path segment above U+007F — a user folder like 王小明 or café — is mangled, so `IsDirectory` fails on directories that exist and `DeleteRecursively` works on a wrong name. In TensorFlow this breaks the flows built on these calls (`isdir`, `makedirs`, `saved_model.save`, `CheckpointManager.save`) for non-ASCII directory names on Windows. Real users hit this in tensorflow/tensorflow#62691 and tensorflow/tensorflow#61550; both were closed as stale without a fix.

**Why**
Non-ASCII user and folder names are the default outside English locales, and saving a model or a checkpoint into such a folder is a basic flow, not an edge case. The reports were closed for staleness, not because the bug went away.

**Design**
Convert with the existing `WideCharToUtf8()` helper instead of the truncating range constructor, in both places (two lines). No other call sites change.

**Testing**
New `EnvTest.NonAsciiDirectoryNames` in `xla/tsl/platform/env_test.cc`: creates `café/王`, checks `RecursivelyCreateDir`, `IsDirectory` on both levels, writes a file, then `DeleteRecursively` and confirms the tree is gone. Reproduced with TensorFlow 2.21.0: the two changed functions return NotFound before and OK after.

One honest limitation: XLA's GitHub CI has no Windows job, so this test's Windows coverage only runs downstream (e.g. TensorFlow's Windows builds). On Linux the test passes either way, since UTF-8 paths are native there.

c6195d503f8dfa91cd36f62366bdcb9980876599 by b84330808 <b84330808@gmail.com>:

[XLA/TSL] Fix WindowsFileSystem::IsDirectory for non-ASCII paths

IsDirectory and DeleteRecursively turned the wide UNC path back into a
std::string by narrowing each wchar_t to a char. For any non-ASCII
character that drops the high byte (U+00E9 becomes 0xE9, U+738B becomes
0x8B), so the FileExists() call that follows looks up a different, invalid
UTF-8 name and fails. Convert with WideCharToUtf8() instead, as the rest of
the file does.

On Windows this made IsDirectory fail for every directory whose path
contains a non-ASCII character, which breaks RecursivelyCreateDir under
such a directory, GetMatchingPaths patterns that recurse into it, Stat's
is_directory, and DeleteRecursively.

Merging this change closes #53038

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build

had to carry one to answer metadata queries.

Move `hlo_module_` and `module_stats_` and the implementations that read them
into `HloModuleExecutable`:

- `shared_module()` (nullable), `module_config()`, `result_shape()`,
  `compute_computation_layout()`, `name()`, `input_output_alias_config()`,
  `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()` are pure virtual on
  `Executable`. `set_module_stats()` lives on `HloModuleExecutable`.
- `module()` and `has_module()` stay as non-virtual helpers on top of a new
  protected pure virtual `module_ptr()`, so they don't copy a
  `std::shared_ptr`.
- Virtuals that don't need state keep their defaults
  (`SizeOfGeneratedCodeInBytes()`, `GetAllocations()`, ...).
- The unused `execution_count_` is deleted.

The only state left in `Executable` is the HLO proto for debugging
(`hlo_proto_` and its mutex). It still fills in the module lazily through
`module()`. Later changes move its producers and readers away and remove it.

`HloModuleExecutable` implements everything from the module as before, so
there is no behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that
derive from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable`
instead (or implement the new pure virtuals).

display_title: Add `is_mutable` parameter to `PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`.

head_commit.message:
Add `is_mutable` parameter to `PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`.

`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` previously hardcoded
`is_mutable=false` when calling `ImportForeignMemory`. GPU ignored the flag,
while `CpuRawBuffer` honored it, so donating a view on PjRt CPU always
allocated a new output buffer instead of aliasing caller memory in place.
Unconditionally flipping `is_mutable` to `true` could surprise callers that
rely on read-only CPU views (such as NumPy or DLPack interop).

Thread an explicit `bool is_mutable` parameter through
`PjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer` (keeping the existing overload
defaulting to `is_mutable=false` for backwards compatibility),
`CommonPjRtClient`, `TfPjRtClient`, `PjRtCApiClient`, and the PJRT C API
v0.119 (`PJRT_Client_CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer_Args::is_mutable`). Callers
that want in-place donation on CPU can opt in with `is_mutable=true`, while
existing callers keep read-only CPU views by default.

Also avoid wrapping an empty `std::function<void()>` (`nullptr`) into a
non-empty `absl::AnyInvocable<void() &&>` in
`CommonPjRtClient::CreateViewOfDeviceBuffer`, which previously threw
`std::bad_function_call` on buffer destruction when `on_delete_callback` was
null.

display_title: [XLA:SDY] Support JAX custom_partitioning in Shardy partitioner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SDY] Support JAX custom_partitioning in Shardy partitioner

When the Shardy partitioner is fully enabled, GSPMD is completely bypassed,
leaving `stablehlo.custom_call @CustomSPMDPartitioning` unpartitioned and
failing compilation. To support it, we change the following:

- **Partitioner-agnostic callback API**: Add
  `CustomCallPartitioner::SupportsMlirPartitioning()` and `PartitionToMlir()`
  (defaulting to `false` / `std::nullopt` for GSPMD-only C++ partitioners),
  share PJRT C-API callback marshaling in `CApiCustomCallPartitioner` between
  GSPMD and Shardy, and remove the now-unused HLO-based `PopulateArgs`
  overload.

- **Callback MLIR preparation & sharding import**: Extract shared tile
  factorization (`factorizeTileAssignmentToSdy`) into
  `stablehlo_round_trip/sharding_import_utils.{h,cc}`, handle matching-mesh V3
  `NamedSharding` directly with V2 fallback, upgrade VHLO, inline direct helper
  calls, and legalize CHLO and complex math in a single `PassManager`, remapping
  positive `channel_handle` IDs via `nextChannelId` and importing remaining
  private helpers (such as `stablehlo.composite` decompositions) into
  `symbolTable`.

- **Global-IR lowering (`resolvePermutationFactors`)**: Wire
  `custom_spmd_partitioning.{h,cc}` into `CustomCallPartitioningOpInterface`,
  rewriting custom-partitioned calls into operand `sdy.reshard` (when needed) +
  divisibility padding + `sdy.manual_computation` + slicing + result
  `sdy.reshard` (when needed).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Generalize IsLargeIndependentFill to sink scalar-parameter fills.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Generalize IsLargeIndependentFill to sink scalar-parameter fills.

Previously, `IsLargeIndependentFill` in
`xla/service/gpu/gpu_latency_hiding_scheduler.cc` required
`instr.operand_count() == 0`, which excluded large (≥ 1 MiB) loop fusions that
broadcast dynamic scalar parameters (such as runtime mask values, step scales,
or tuple-unpacked scalar arguments). Because those fusions have
`AsyncDepth == 0`, the bottom-up latency-hiding scheduler deferred them behind
`while` loops and collective regions, floating their multi-megabyte output
buffers to the top of the computation.

Generalize `IsLargeIndependentFill` via `HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands` to
accept loop fusions whose operands are all effective scalars that are constants
or effective parameters (`hlo_query::IsEffectiveParameter`). Because constant
and effective-parameter scalar operands have zero upstream compute or
collective dependencies and negligible live buffer footprints, marking these
fills `ForceEarly(true)` sinks them next to their consumers without delaying
async collective starts. On a 512x512 `f32` (1 MiB) broadcast fill consumed
after a `while` loop, this reduces peak live memory pressure from 3 MiB to
2 MiB (-33%) while preserving the full 1,002-cycle `while` and `all-reduce`
overlap.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Sink large broadcast fills from scalar cones and small parameters.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Sink large broadcast fills from scalar cones and small parameters.

Previously, `IsLargeIndependentFill` (`HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands`)
required every operand of a large (≥ 1 MiB) `kLoop` fusion to be a direct
scalar constant or effective parameter. Consequently, the GPU latency-hiding
scheduler did not mark broadcast fills `ForceEarly(true)` when their scalar
operand was produced by pure scalar arithmetic (such as negating or scaling a
runtime scalar argument) or when they broadcast a small non-scalar parameter
(such as a 2 KiB parameter vector into a 1 MiB matrix). Because these fusions
have `AsyncDepth == 0`, bottom-up scheduling deferred them behind `while` loops
and collective regions, floating their multi-megabyte output buffers to the top
of the computation.

Replace `HasOnlyIndependentScalarOperands` with
`HasOnlyIndependentAmplifiedOperands` and `IsIndependentScalarSubgraph` in
`IsLargeIndependentFill` so the scheduler also sinks large (≥ 1 MiB) loop
fusions whose inputs are amplified by at least 100x
(`kMinFillAmplificationFactor = 100`) and consist solely of constants,
effective parameters, or bounded synchronous scalar ancestor cones
(`kMaxScalarConeNodes = 16` elementwise, bitcast, or reshape instructions).
Requiring every node in a computed operand's ancestor cone to be a synchronous
effective scalar guarantees zero collective async depth (`AsyncDepth == 0`)
before `InitializeGraphAnalysis` runs and prevents sinking fusions whose scalar
operand derives from reducing or slicing a large upstream tensor, which would
extend the upstream tensor's live range. On a 1 MiB (`f32[512,512]`) broadcast
fill fed by a negated scalar parameter across a `while` loop, sinking the fill
right before its consumer reduces scheduled peak live memory by 33.3% (from
3.00 MiB to 2.00 MiB).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Rematerialize copies of large iota fills in ConstantFillCopyRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Rematerialize copies of large iota fills in ConstantFillCopyRewriter.

When `CopyInsertion` duplicates a 0-operand `kIota` loop fusion (for example,
when an index tensor initializes a `while` loop carry and also feeds a consumer
outside the loop), `CopyFusion` folds the `kCopy` into the original fusion as a
multi-output tuple. That couples the two live ranges together at the earliest
consumer's timestamp and keeps the copied buffer live across the intervening
loop.

Extend `ConstantFillCopyRewriter` (`IsConstantOrIotaFillBody` in
`xla/backends/gpu/transforms/constant_fill_copy_rewriter.cc`) to recognize
0-operand `kIota` loop fusions (≥ 1 MiB) alongside scalar-constant broadcasts.
Replacing each `kCopy` with an independent 0-operand `kIota` fusion eliminates
the device-to-device HBM read at the copy site (cutting memory traffic for that
buffer by 50%, since `iota` synthesizes indices in registers) and allows the
scheduler to sink the rematerialized fill next to its consumer, reducing
scheduled peak live memory by the full buffer size (e.g., 1 MiB for an
`s32[512,512]` index grid).

display_title: Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

head_commit.message:
Add HloModuleExecutable and derive the OSS executables from it

The goal is to avoid loading the `HloModule` when an executable is loaded in
an AOT setup. Deserializing the module is expensive, and a loaded executable
only needs it for debugging (dumps, profiling, introspection). But today
`Executable` owns the `HloModule` and answers metadata queries (module config,
entry computation layout, input/output aliasing, ...) from it, so every
backend and every caller depends on the module being there.

So `Executable` is going to become an abstract base class without data
members. Executables that keep the HloModule they were compiled from derive
from a new `HloModuleExecutable`, which implements today's behaviour.
Executables that don't need the module at runtime (like `GpuExecutable` for
loaded AOT executables) can then implement the interface without it.

As a first step this adds `HloModuleExecutable` in
`xla/service/hlo_module_executable.h`. For now it only forwards the
constructor to `Executable`; the module related members move there in a
follow-up.

`GpuExecutable`, `CpuExecutable`, `InterpreterExecutableBase` and the test
fakes in `xla/service/executable_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/gpu_profiler_test.cc`,
`xla/backends/autotuner/autotuner_test.cc` and
`xla/backends/autotuner/config_runner_test.cc` now derive from
`HloModuleExecutable` instead of `Executable`.

No behaviour change.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Support temporary buffers larger than the page size in multi page buffer assignment

Multi page buffer assignment previously failed a check whenever a temporary buffer exceeded `page_size_kib`. With `round_up_oversized_heaps`, `ConstrainedGlobalDecreasingSizeBestFitHeap` rounds an oversized heap limit up to a multiple of the page size. Only non zero buffers that also need all of those pages join that heap. For `BufferAssignment::kPagingColor`, `AssignBuffersFromHeapSimulator` places single page heaps first and assigns consecutive page IDs. `CombineTempAllocations` reserves consecutive page IDs across `kPagingColor` allocations and keeps combined allocations within one page.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Verify element types, devices, and memory kind for `io_aliases`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Verify devices, memory kind, and per-shard byte size for `io_aliases`

Aliasing an input to an output on `ifrt.Call` and `ifrt.CallLoadedExecutable` requires the two buffers to reside on the same devices and memory kind, while allowing different element types, per-shard shapes, and layouts as long as their per-shard byte size matches. Enforcing only element-type and per-shard-shape equality missed impossible cross-device and host-to-device aliases while rejecting valid bitcast-style or layout-changing aliases.

`IfrtCallOpInterface` verification now requires XLA array element types (rejecting `!ifrt.token` and `!ifrt.string`), matching devices, matching effective memory kinds, and valid user-specified layouts (via `xla::ShapeUtil::ValidateShape`), and drops the element-type and per-shard-shape equality requirements.

When both shardings are specified and both layouts are default (including omitted `layout`) or both are untiled user-specified, verification checks per-shard byte-size equality via `xla::ShapeUtil::ArraySize`. Byte-size verification for tiled, `auto`, and mixed (`default`/user-specified) layouts—and for pairs with unspecified sharding—is deferred to atom-program compilation (e.g., XLA after layout assignment) or the underlying IFRT runtime for externally bound executables.

Also updates `ProgramInterpreter` and `ProgramMemoryTracer` to use the `IfrtCallOpInterface` alias helpers (`GetDonatedOrAliasedInputIndices` and `getIoAliasPairs`) instead of unpacking raw `io_aliases` attributes, and adds memory-tracer test coverage for aliased arrays with differing dtypes, shapes, and layouts.

display_title: [XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

Whether a computation is embedded cannot be determined from its direct callers
alone: a `while`, `conditional`, or `call` body inside a `map`, `sort`, or
`reduce` has a `CallContext::kControlFlow` direct caller even though it executes
inside an embedded computation. `CallGraph` already computes transitive
`CallContext` in one pass over the module.

- Add `CallGraphNode::IsEmbedded()` to check whether a computation is in an
  embedded context (`CallContext::kEmbedded` or `CallContext::kBoth`).
- Use `CallGraphNode::IsEmbedded()` in `InstructionFusion`, `MultiOutputFusion`,
  and `EmbeddedWhileLoopUnroller` instead of
  `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.
- Add `ScatterExpander::kEliminateEmbeddedScatters` backed by `CallGraph` and
  use it in `CpuCompiler` so transitively embedded scatters are expanded too.
- Remove `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.

Note on behavior change: this is not purely a refactor for non-CPU backends.
Control-flow bodies nested inside embedded computations (e.g. a `while`,
`conditional`, or `call` inside a `reduce`/`sort`/`map` body) were previously
fused by `InstructionFusion` and `MultiOutputFusion` on GPU/TPU and now will not
be.

display_title: Derive GpuExecutable from Executable directly

head_commit.message:
Derive GpuExecutable from Executable directly

`GpuExecutable` now derives from the abstract `Executable` instead of
`HloModuleExecutable`. It keeps its optional `HloModule` and its `ModuleStats`
itself and implements `shared_module()`, `module_config()`,
`input_output_alias_config()`, `buffer_donor_config()` and `module_stats()`.

If the executable has the module, these return the module's values, exactly as
before. Without the module (`embed_hlo_module=false`, or a `GpuExecutableProto`
without a serialized module), the executable answers from what it keeps:

- The input/output aliasing is rebuilt from the output info, which is already
  part of `GpuExecutableProto`.
- `module_config()` and `buffer_donor_config()` come from the new
  `GpuExecutable::Params::module_config` and `Params::buffer_donor_config`,
  which `GpuCompiler` fills from the module when it doesn't embed it.
  `module_config()` still CHECK-fails if neither is there, as today.

This way callers can get the metadata of an executable compiled with
`embed_hlo_module=false` through the `Executable` interface, and
`GpuExecutable` no longer needs `HloModuleExecutable`.

PR #53299: [XLA:GPU] Auto-enable keeping recorded collectives out of output allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53299

📝 Summary of Changes

`xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` is now enabled automatically when `COLLECTIVES` is in `xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the command buffer update mode is `SKIP_TEMP` or `SKIP_PROFILED`. In any other configuration it stays disabled. An explicit value of the flag takes priority.

This is the follow-up to https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52104, which added the flag with default off.

🎯 Justification

In these modes a collective whose buffer shares an output allocation is re-recorded on every execution. The flag avoids that at the cost of some temp memory. Users who select these modes should get this without knowing about a second flag.

72c0c434e968b61d917b8a800096a926a15004d1 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Keep recorded collectives out of output allocations by default

Flip the default of
`xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` to true.

The flag only takes effect with COLLECTIVES in
`xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED command
buffer update mode. In that configuration a collective whose buffer shares
an output allocation is re-recorded on every execution, because the output
allocation gets a new address each time. Keeping these buffers in the temp
allocation gives them a stable address, so the recorded collective is
skipped at initialization.

The default configuration (ALWAYS_UPDATE, COLLECTIVES not in command
buffers) is unchanged. Setting the flag to false restores the previous
behavior.

--
fb92f6f2cd2378c767b79b09615fb97a82df8858 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Auto-enable keeping collectives out of outputs from presence

Leave `xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs` unset by
default instead of defaulting it to true. When it is not set, it is
enabled with COLLECTIVES in `xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` and the
SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED update mode, and disabled otherwise. An
explicit value takes priority.

--
133df5762d94d5a4cfffbde646ac081d9a4f7aa5 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Make an explicit keep-collectives-out-of-outputs value always win

When xla_gpu_command_buffer_keep_collectives_out_of_outputs is unset it is
enabled automatically if COLLECTIVES is in xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer and
the update mode is SKIP_TEMP or SKIP_PROFILED, and disabled otherwise. An
explicit true or false now takes priority in every configuration.

The resolution lives in one helper returning a Decision. GetNonDefaultDebugOptions
now also compares presence for fields with explicit presence, so an explicit
false is kept in *.debug_options dumps instead of being dropped as equal to the
unset default. The flag help and proto comment describe the three states.

PR #53334: [XLA:GPU] Squeeze single-row reductions in TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53334

📝 Summary of Changes
TritonXLASqueezeDimsPass now also squeezes a tt.reduce over a [1, N] row tile:
it becomes a 1D reduce plus tt.splat, so the row stays in one layout.

display_title: PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

head_commit.message:
PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

This adds `NcclCommunicator::Split()`, which waits on the parent until the split finishes and only then returns the child. `Abort()` cancels a pending split wait, so it can't deadlock on the parent mutex. If a split fails with an uncertain outcome, the child-handle storage is intentionally left allocated, since NCCL may still write to it.

🎯 Justification

Recoverable JAX jobs that use nonblocking communicators and communicator splitting can fail, and later crash, when XLA uses an uninitialized child.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

  Added regression tests:

- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitCommunicatorsNonblocking: a nonblocking split returns valid, healthy communicators.
- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitAbortedCommunicatorsFails: splitting an aborted communicator fails with a clear error.

🧪 Execution Tests:

N/A in XLA.

ae55c49f8ea4faa8b3c67b7b4c1d714dc60d4fd0 by Jane Liu <janeliu@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, ncclCommSplit can return before the
child handle is published. XLA read the output immediately, so it could
see a NULL child, and NCCL could later write to a stack variable that no
longer existed.

Add NcclCommunicator::Split(), which keeps the output on the heap and
polls the parent with ncclCommGetAsyncError until the split completes
before returning the child. If the wait fails or the child is
unexpectedly NULL, the output storage is leaked with a warning, since
NCCL may still write to it. Reclaiming it after parent teardown is left
for a follow-up.

from it too.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Remove Executable::hlo_proto_ and make Executable an abstract base class

head_commit.message:
Remove Executable::hlo_proto_ and make Executable an abstract base class

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule. `hlo_proto_` (with its mutex) is the last data member of
`Executable`, and all its producers and readers have moved away:

- Backends override the virtual `buffer_assignment_proto()` with state they
  own.
- HLO snapshots use the HLO that `Service` or `LocalExecutable` keep, or
  `MakeHloProtoForSnapshot()`.
- `DumpingHloSnapshots()` replaces `dumping_snapshot()`.

So remove `set_hlo_proto()`, `hlo_proto()`, `dumping_snapshot()`, `hlo_proto_`
and its mutex. With that, `Executable` is an abstract base class without data
members, and `buffer_assignment_proto()` becomes pure virtual.
`HloModuleExecutable` returns nullptr, the backends that keep a buffer
assignment override it.

No behaviour change for executables in XLA. Out-of-tree backends that derive
from `Executable` directly have to derive from `HloModuleExecutable` instead
(or implement the pure virtuals).

display_title: Stop calling Executable::set_hlo_proto in the GPU and CPU compilers

head_commit.message:
Stop calling Executable::set_hlo_proto in the GPU and CPU compilers

Overarching goal: loading an AOT-compiled executable shouldn't need to build
the HloModule, and `Executable` becomes an abstract base class without data
members. The GPU and CPU compilers only attached an `HloProto` so that the
base class could answer `buffer_assignment_proto()` and so that HLO snapshots
had something to read. `GpuExecutable` and `CpuExecutable` now override
`buffer_assignment_proto()` themselves, and snapshots no longer read
`Executable::hlo_proto()`, so the compilers stop calling `set_hlo_proto`.

`Executable::hlo_proto()` now returns nullptr for GPU and CPU executables. No
caller in XLA reads it anymore. `buffer_assignment_proto()` returns the same as
before.

display_title: [TFLite YNNPACK] Lower MoE experts with ragged_dot and blockwise quantization.

head_commit.message:
[TFLite YNNPACK] Lower MoE experts with ragged_dot and blockwise quantization.
Previously, `DefineMoeNode` split MoE execution between host-side padded token bucketing (`[E, C, D]`) for multi-token prefill when `expert_indices` was a partition input and a weight-gather fallback for single-token decode or partition-internal `expert_indices`, which copied selected expert weights per token and prevented static `pack_b` and column-sum constant folding on blockwise-quantized weights.
- Unify `DefineMoeNode` in the TFLite YNNPACK delegate to lower `odml.moe_experts` ops (decode and prefill, symmetric `AffineQuantization`, `MultiAxisQuantization`, and `BlockwiseQuantization` in `int8` and `int4`) via `ynn_define_ragged_dot` and `ynn::define_blockwise_dot` over host-partitioned `[B * N * K, D]` expert slots and stationary 3D `[E, D_in, D_out]` weights.
- Trace partition-internal `RESHAPE` and `EXPAND_DIMS` views on `expert_indices` back to the external partition input (or constant) tensor, while rejecting MoE nodes whose `expert_indices` is produced by non-view partition ops.
- Flatten the MoE combine reduction from 4D `[B, N, K, D_out]` to 3D `[B * N, K, D_out]` followed by `ynn_define_split_dim` back to `[B, N, D_out]`, avoiding an outer loop over `B` and skipping YNNPACK subgraph rebuilds in `Prepare` when only sequence length `N` changes.
- Replace padded host token bucketing in `MoeDispatch`, `SetupMoeDispatch`, and `SetMoeDispatchShapes` with flat slot partitioning, removing `ShouldDispatchMoeOnHost`, `SetMoeDispatchData`, and `dispatch_moe_on_host`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Move the XLA:CPU builtin symbols to an LLVM-free target

head_commit.message:
Move the XLA:CPU builtin symbols to an LLVM-free target

The table of host functions that XLA:CPU kernels can call (libm, fp16 and bf16 conversions, __powisf2, ...) lives inside `BuiltinDefinitionGenerator`, which is an ORC definition generator, so loaders that don't use ORC can't reuse it.

So we move the table to `:builtin_symbols` (`FindBuiltinSymbol`), which doesn't depend on LLVM, and `BuiltinDefinitionGenerator` looks names up there. That way ORC and `LiteObjectLoader` (next CLs) resolve exactly the same symbols.
